title: Senior Platform Engineer, Growth Product Engineering
description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Are you a platform engineer who wants to build the foundation that lets an entire growth product engineering organization move faster? At Samsara, we are looking for a Senior Platform Engineer to join Growth Product & Engineering and own the platform our growth and marketing teams build on. As we push toward AI-assisted and agentic development, our velocity is increasingly bottlenecked not by feature work but by foundational gaps in infrastructure, security, and tooling. These initiatives cut across every team, but no single person owns them today. You will.

This is a hands-on, high-leverage role. You will design the hardened CI/CD pipeline that makes agent-written code safe to ship, migrate hand-built AWS resources to Infrastructure as Code, isolate production and pre-production workloads into properly separated accounts, centralize logging and monitoring, and give every engineer a paved path to self-service infrastructure. Our stack includes Python, JavaScript (Vue), AWS, and GitHub Actions (workflow) API with a growing surface of serverless and container based services and internally hosted applications.

The core principle behind this work: when a human writes a PR, the human is the safety net; when an AI agent writes a PR, the pipeline is the safety net. Raising that bar is the prerequisite for scaling AI-assisted development safely, and it is the single highest-leverage investment we can make in engineering velocity. If that excites you, we would love to talk.

This role is open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are energized by leverage: You would rather build the systems that prevent an entire class of problems than fix the same problem ten times.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role will not be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development and countless opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the CI/CD foundation for AI-assisted and agentic development: hardened pipeline gates, high test coverage, mutation and end-to-end tests, blocking security scans, performance and cost regression guards, and progressive delivery with automated rollback.
  • Give engineers a fast, safe inner loop with ephemeral per-PR environments and local tooling, including isolated databases seeded from realistic data.
  • Build centralized logging, monitoring, and alerting across our AWS footprint so every team has visibility and bad deployments roll back automatically.
  • Lead security engineering: remediate vulnerabilities, establish secure-by-default patterns, and automate code scanning, secrets management, and access control.
  • Migrate hand-built AWS resources to Infrastructure as Code, separate production and pre-production accounts, and stand up tested backup and disaster recovery with clear RTO and RPO targets.
  • Build paved-path, self-service tooling and standardized blue/green, canary, and feature-flag releases, while mentoring engineers and role modeling Samsara’s cultural principles as we scale.
  • Build and operate AI agents for SRE work: automated alert triage, incident investigation, and safe self-healing remediation, so on-call toil drops as our service footprint grows.
  • Contribute to backend development for products: assist with backend cloud services product work, shipping customer-facing features alongside the platform, not just internal tooling.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 6+ years of professional software, infrastructure, DevOps, platform, or site reliability engineering experience.
  • Hands-on AWS production experience (IAM, Lambda, networking, and multi-account organizations) with Infrastructure as Code such as Terraform, AWS CDK, or CloudFormation.
  • Designed and operated CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, buildkite) with automated testing, static analysis, coverage enforcement, and deployment gates, plus safe release patterns such as blue/green, canary, feature flags, and reliable rollbacks. We use GitHub Actions workflows for CI/CD.
  • Strong Python development experience across services, tooling, and automation, working familiarity with JavaScript-based stacks, and experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker with ECS, EKS, or Kubernetes).
  • Cloud security posture management (CSPM) or our tools like Wiz, semgrep, synk, etc.
  • Experience building observability into distributed systems: centralized logging, metrics, tracing, and alerting (for example Sentry, Datadog, CloudWatch, or Grafana).
  • Track record of designing, building, and operating production infrastructure end to end with measurable gains in reliability, security, or developer velocity, using AI-powered development tools (for example Claude, Cursor, Codex, or Copilot) in a daily workflow.
  • Experience with product and feature development: building and shipping customer-facing product features, not just internal platform and infrastructure work.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience building the guardrails that make AI or agent-generated code safe to merge and deploy: mutation testing, coverage enforcement, ephemeral preview environments, or automated rollback.
  • A developer experience or platform engineering background, with a track record of paved-path tooling that other engineers actually adopt.
  • Familiarity with cloud cost management, performance regression detection, capacity planning, and disaster recovery plans rehearsed against measured RTO and RPO targets.
  • Exposure to localization pipelines and to GTM or data tooling such as Salesforce, Contentful, Hightouch, or Databricks, plus an experiment-driven approach to adopting emerging AI technologies.
  • Experience with Service Level Indicators (SLIs) and Service Level Objectives (SLOs) as the foundation for observability in our system.
  • Own our operational review process and always look for ways to make it better.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$131,792—$199,350 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

title: Printing Press Operator - Assistant
description:
We are the people who give possibilities purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.





Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Assists Flexographic Printing Press Operator by:

  • Checking quality and correctness of printing mats, properly setting up, aligning, and affixing printing mats to printing sleeves or mandrel.

  • Inspecting the raw materials to ensure the correct web stock and ink are being used for top webs to be processed.

  • Placing roll of web material stock on press and checking web material for correctness.

  • Operating the printing press in such a manner as to process a high quality product.

  • Performing cleanup and preventative maintenance of printing and slitting equipment in accordance with equipment manuals and Quality Control requirements.

  • Making repairs on printing and slitting equipment and assisting Tool Room or Maintenance on major repairs.

  • Performing inventory control and recording of printing inks, printing mats and paper stock used in the printing of web materials.

  • Performing internal scheduling of web material to be processed to maintain an efficient operation with minimum of down time for all changeovers.

title: Senior / Lead Subsea Pipeline Engineer
description:
Wood is looking for an experienced Senior or Lead Subsea Pipeline Engineer to join our team in Norway. We have subsea hub offices in Stavanger and Oslo.

You'll become part of a team of close to 60 engineers in Norway and work closely with colleagues across the region. We support projects within oil and gas and energy transition, from early studies through detailed engineering, execution and operation. The role is based in Norway, and applicants must currently live and work in Norway.

Your role

In this role, you'll contribute to the delivery of subsea pipeline solutions for a range of clients and projects. Wood is currently executing some of the most challenging pipeline projects on the Norwegian shelf, including HPHT, deep water, uneven seabeds, and large diameter export infrastructure.

Your responsibilities will typically include:

  • Providing pipeline expertise to project and operations teams, with DNV standards typically governing our work.
  • Performing pipeline design activities in close collaboration with SPS, Subsea Structures and Systems disciplines.
  • Supporting and mentoring junior subsea pipeline engineers.
  • Contributing to project risk workshops and design reviews, identifying and following up risks, opportunities and associated actions.

Is this you?

You're an experienced and proactive subsea pipeline engineer who enjoys taking ownership, solving technical challenges and working closely with clients and colleagues to deliver high-quality engineering solutions.

You have a relevant engineering degree, solid experience within subsea pipeline engineering and a good understanding of DNV standards. Previous experience on the Norwegian Continental Shelf is strongly preferred.

Experience in some or all of the following areas is required: mechanical design, wall thickness and coatings, freespans, buckling, pipe-soil interaction, installation engineering, and pipeline protection.

Experience with ANSYS, ABAQUS, OrcaFlex, Navimodel or similar tools is important.

Why join Wood?

Professional development: We actively encourage professional growth through mentoring, knowledge sharing and technical guidance. You will be connected to one of the world’s largest groups of technical experts. You'll also have opportunities for site visits, project placements and exposure to related disciplines, helping you broaden both your technical expertise and understanding of project delivery.

A collaborative culture: We're proud of the environment we've built in Wood. People are approachable, willing to share knowledge and committed to helping one another succeed. We believe the best solutions come from collaboration and strong teamwork.

What we offer: Alongside a competitive salary package and strong pension and insurance schemes, we offer flexible working hours with core hours from 09:00 to 15:00, modern office facilities, a well-subsidised canteen, fitness facilities and plenty of on-site parking. You'll also be part of an active social environment with sports teams and events throughout the year.

Interested?

Think this could be the right next step for you? We'd love to hear from you. Please include a short, personal cover letter explaining your relevant experience and motivation for the role.

We review applications continuously and encourage candidates to apply as early as possible.

title: Senior Business Analyst - Workforce Planning (12mth FTC)
description:
ASX: Powering Australia's financial markets

Why join the ASX?

When you join ASX, you’re joining a company with a strong purpose – to power a stronger economic future by enabling a fair and dynamic marketplace for all.

www.asx.com.au/about/careers/a-great-place-to-work

Your responsibilities

  • Lead business analysis across Position Management, Workforce Planning and Financial Planning to support the end-to-end implementation and adoption of Workday Adaptive Planning for P&C.
  • Work with impacted stakeholders to perform deep dive gap analysis on the As-Is state and the To Be State, allowing for effective review by project team members and impacted stakeholders.
  • Liaise with assigned Project/Program Owners and Subject Matter Experts for elicitation, analysis, prioritisation and approval of new business requests within associated projects.
  • Define transitions of business processes to the strategic state, with interim/tactical states where needed, including the connected operating model, roles, accountabilities, governance, controls and decision rights required for workforce and financial planning.
  • Analyse and map process flows, domain models, system data flows and associated life cycle events to determine and manage transition to the target state.
  • Elicit, prepare and manage business requirements, including functional and non-functional requirements, in the form of epics, features, user stories and acceptance criteria, and clearly articulate these to developers, testers, vendors and project stakeholders.
  • Define and validate data, reporting, planning, security and integration requirements across Workday HCM, Position Management, Workday Adaptive Planning and related systems.
  • Use formal modelling techniques to assist in the representation of business requirements.
  • Liaise with counterparts in related internal project/domain teams to understand dependencies, constraints and associated requirements, and agree upon and deliver solutions. Maintain clear links between requirements, risks, decisions and delivery outcomes across P&C, Finance, Technology and implementation partners.
  • Review and contribute to specific test scenarios and the overall Test Strategy, and lead business validation and readiness for user acceptance testing.
  • Liaise with IT solution providers, internal and external, on project progress, requirements clarification and problem resolution.

  • Work with Release Management to ensure a smooth implementation and transition phase.
  • Contribution to change management activities and preparation of training artefacts that would enable impacted stakeholders to apply the changes introduced by a delivered business requirement.

  • Produce high-quality business analysis deliverables using relevant techniques and tools in line with the ASX delivery framework

Your experience and qualifications

Must have

  • Experience working independently on Tier 1 projects across the full SDLC from early ideation to execution and embedment in BAU.

  • Experience in gathering stakeholder needs and translating these to detailed functional and non-functional requirements.
  • Experience analysing and designing integrated processes, operating models, governance, controls and data requirements across Position Management, Workforce Planning or Financial Planning.
  • Experience in business process modelling using software such as MS Visio or other enterprise endorsed platforms.
  • Experience using Atlassian tool suite, including JIRA and Confluence.
  • Effective communication, facilitation, influencing and negotiation skills. Can collaborate with stakeholders across seniority levels and lead cross-functional analysis across P&C, Finance and Technology.
  • Demonstrated effective problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve competing requirements and manage change within a dynamic environment.

Nice to have

title: Plant Operator - Renewable Power (C&C)
description:
About OPAL Fuels
OPAL Fuels (Nasdaq: OPAL) is a leader in the capture and conversion of biogas into low carbon intensity RNG and renewable electricity. OPAL Fuels is also a leader in the marketing and distribution of RNG to heavy duty trucking and other hard to de-carbonize industrial sectors. For additional information, and to learn more about OPAL Fuels and how it is leading the effort to capture North America’s naturally occurring methane and decarbonize the economy, please visit www.opalfuels.com.

Position Summary
We are hiring for a Plant Operator to work in our Renewable Power Plant. The Plant Operator/Generator Mechanic is responsible for the safe, reliable, and efficient day‑to‑day operation and maintenance of a landfill‑gas‑to‑energy facility consisting of one gas turbine and two Waukesha LFG engines. This position reports to the Area Manager and shares accountability for equipment performance, regulatory compliance, and overall site operations. The primary objectives are to maximize production, minimize downtime, and uphold the highest standards of safety, cleanliness, and environmental stewardship.

Duties and Responsibilities

Plant Operations & Monitoring
  • Operate, monitor, and maintain the gas turbine, Waukesha engines, gas compressors, and auxiliary equipment.
  • Perform daily inspections of flow meters, gas chromatographs, pressures, temperatures, vibration indicators, alarms, and abnormal noises.
  • Start, stop, and adjust plant equipment according to operational requirements and approved procedures.
  • Monitor engine and turbine performance to ensure optimal output and reliability.
Maintenance & Reliability
  • Perform preventive maintenance and corrective repairs on turbines, engines, compressors, pumps, blowers, and support systems.
  • Conduct oil and filter changes, coolant service, lubrication, belt and hose replacement, valve and seal changes, bearing replacements, and other mechanical repairs.
  • Participate in scheduled preventive maintenance outages and major overhauls.
  • Maintain accurate records of production data, run hours, maintenance activities, service schedules, and equipment outages.
Housekeeping & Site Standards
  • Maintain a high level of cleanliness throughout the plant.
  • Prevent oil and fluid accumulation on skids, floors, and surrounding soil; clean spills immediately.
  • Keep plant yards, walkways, and perimeter fencing clear of weeds, vegetation, and debris.
  • Maintain a professional, organized, and safe work environment.
Inventory & Materials Management
  • Maintain onsite spare parts, tools, and consumables in an organized inventory system.
  • Monitor inventory levels and communicate material needs to ensure uninterrupted operations.
  • Report low‑stock or critical‑stock conditions to support procurement planning.
Safety & Environmental Compliance
  • Operate the facility with continuous focus on safety and environmental stewardship.
  • Ensure lighting, walkways, and safety systems are functional and free of hazards.
  • Identify, report, and correct electrical, mechanical, or environmental hazards promptly.
  • Ensure visitors, contractors, and maintenance personnel follow safe work practices.
  • Adhere to all company policies, operating procedures, and regulatory requirements.
Communication & Coordination
  • Communicate equipment status, operational issues, material needs, and personnel concerns promptly to the Area Manager.
  • Document operational changes, maintenance activities, and call‑out responses.
  • Coordinate with contractors, mechanics, and landfill personnel as needed.
Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement
  • Assist in equipment failure investigations and root cause analysis.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on reliability, efficiency, and safety.
  • Contribute to the development, review, and revision of SOPs and maintenance procedures.
Fuel Quality & Landfill Coordination
  • Monitor landfill gas quality (BTU content, pressure, moisture, contaminants).
  • Report deviations affecting turbine or engine performance.
  • Coordinate with landfill personnel to resolve gas supply or quality issues.
Training & Skill Development
  • Assist with onboarding and training of new Plant Operators.
  • Maintain required qualifications, certifications, and safety/environmental training.
  • Support knowledge sharing and skill development within the operations team.
On‑Call & Call‑Out Responsibilities
  • Participate in an on‑call rotation providing off‑hours, weekend, and holiday coverage.
  • Respond promptly to alarms, call‑outs, and emergency notifications.
  • Diagnose and correct operational or equipment issues when possible.
  • Escalate unresolved or complex issues to the Area Manager or additional support resources.
  • Document call‑out responses, corrective actions, and follow‑up requirements.

Qualifications and Skills

  • High school diploma/ GED equivalent
  • Minimum three years of heavy equipment operations experience (gas turbine, reciprocating engines, or gas compressors preferred).
  • Strong mechanical aptitude; basic electrical knowledge preferred.
  • General troubleshooting abilities.
  • Skilled in recordkeeping and logging.
  • Ability to read and write effectively.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
  • Self‑motivated and able to work with minimal supervision.
  • Working knowledge of pressure, vacuum, and flow systems.
  • Experience with pumps, blowers, or air compressors.
  • Valid, unrestricted driver’s license.

Work Hours and Arrangements

Monday to Thursday; 7:00 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. On call every other week (rotating), Monday to Monday, 7:00 p.m. – 7:00 a.m.

Physical Requirements
The physical demands described are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Moderate lifting (10–50 lbs.), occasional walking on irregular surfaces, stooping, kneeling, climbing, or crouching. Use of hands and arms required for operating or examining gas meters, flow meters, hand tools, power tools, cranes, and diagnostic equipment. Position also requires driving motorized vehicles, operating an ATV, and computer work.

Job Type
Full-time

Pay
The range for this role is anticipated to be $35.00 - $38.00 hourly with bonus for eligible positions. Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.

Benefits
  • Health Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • Short & Long Term Disability
  • 401(k) plus Matching Contributions
  • Tuition Assistance
  • Referral Bonus
  • Generous Paid Time Off
  • Ten Paid Holidays per year

title: Delivery Manager
description:
Delivery Manager

Delivery Manager

Role Overview

Delivery Manager is the high-level role within a tribe responsible for the cross-squad delivery management. It is analogues to Release Train Engineer (RTE) as defined in SAFe framework. Role takes charge of defining delivery scope, coordinating squads to deliver value and act as a chief Scrum Master to ensure development process is managed optimally.

This role directly manages team of Scrum Masters within a tribe, and works closely with PMO tribe, to provide centralized governance on Tribe’s SDLC and Ways of Working.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Manage and optimize the flow of value through the cross-platform releases;
  • Establish and communicate the annual calendars for Iterations and Program Increments (PIs);
  • Facilitate PI planning, tribe-wide backlog refinement, and roadmap preparation;
  • Assist tracking the execution of features and capabilities;
  • Facilitate periodic synchronization events as necessary throughout development process;
  • Ensure that leaders, teams, and Scrum Masters follow agile practices and mindsets. Where necessary, provide support and training on organizational-wide agreed standards and practices;
  • Work with tribe leadership, and other stakeholders to help ensure strategy and execution alignment;
  • Handle communication and collaboration with other tribes to identify risks, effectively remove impediments and resolve dependencies;
  • Support and collaborate with Head of Engineering of a tribe to define and track the roadmap;
  • Support and collaborate with Head of Engineering of a tribe to prepare quarterly reviews;
  • Track agile metrics for the tribe and all its squads and review them with relevant stakeholders;
  • Implement and manage agile SDLC process and relevant tooling across the platform to improve efficiency and maximize value;
  • Directly manage Scrum Masters of the tribe. This includes regular 1 to 1s, performance management, mentoring, guidance and probation follow through.
  • Participate in the recruitment process to hire Scrum Masters for the squad. The focus will be on the human and cultural aspects.
  • Liaise with Solution Architects early or prior to new platform-wide solution implementation to get alignment on technical approaches;
  • Ensure the teams are set up and delivering on their roadmap alligned to Singulars Vision & Mission;
  • Liase with Operations teams to ensure problems, incidents & bugs are also getting roadmap time and there is a balance between new features and operating our products to agreed SLA’s
  • Provide leadership and direction where necessary:
  • Implement team goals or objectives;
  • Supervise, train or guide team members;
  • Mediate any interpersonal issues;
  • Inspire and motivate team members;
  • Provide effective feedback;
  • Manage remote teams.
  • Related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Working Experience:

  • 5+ Delivery/Project/Programme Management Experience;
  • Experience working with SaaS products;
  • Experience with iterative, value-driven product releases;
  • Experience working with cross functional teams in a technology domain.

Standard Qualifications:

  • Proficiency with Atlassian tools (especially JIRA & Confluence);
  • Good understanding of Agile frameworks and their differences;
  • Proficiency in formal communication;
  • Proficiency with common collaboration tools: Google Docs, Slack, Skype;
  • Advanced level of English Language;

Preferable Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of SAFe framework;
  • Development or QA background;
  • Knowledge of software QA methodologies and experience with test plan implementation;
  • Proficiency in designing sequence diagrams, activity diagrams, flowcharts;
  • ITIL Certification.

Certification:

  • Professional Scrum Master (PSM) Certificate 1/2/3

Personal Attributes

  • Highly developed leadership skills;
  • Highly developed presentation skills;
  • Analytical mindset with strong reasoning skills;
  • Excellent comprehension skills;
  • Sharp mind, fast thinker;
  • Strong Organizational and time management skills;
  • Strong negotiation skills;
  • Strong Problem-solving skills;
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills;
  • Ability to work under pressure.

Career Path

  • Head of Delivery
  • Director of Delivery

description:
Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Our community is a close-knit group of remarkable individuals driven by intellectual inquiry, a commitment to social justice, and a shared dedication to making a difference in the world.

Requirements

Job Overview

The Project Manager plays a vital role in supporting the university mission by ensuring the delivery of high-quality campus design and construction capital projects. This position manages the planning, execution, and close-out of assigned projects, serving as a key liaison between internal partners, external consultants, and contractors. Reporting to the Planning and Capital Projects department, the individual manages multiple projects concurrently with budget values typically ranging from five thousand dollars to five million dollars, but could be higher.

Responsibilities include leading projects from the design concept stage through construction documents, bidding, and construction administration to final turnover. The Project Manager provides direction and coordination for project teams composed of clients, architects, engineers, and operations personnel. They are responsible for obtaining necessary approvals from internal entities and government agencies while ensuring all work adheres to project budgets, schedules, and university standards.

The Project Manager conducts regular on-site inspections to evaluate contractor performance and confirm the satisfactory progression of work. Throughout all phases of construction, the Project Manager ensures that work is performed in alignment with the university living wage policy for construction work, serving as a resource to help vendors meet labor accountability standards. The role may also involve designing small projects, supporting master planning efforts, and developing reports and presentations using design and planning software. Special assignments may require technical problem-solving and cross-functional collaboration. Performs special project activities requiring application of technical expertise to the development of solutions to unusually difficult problems, as assigned.

Performs project management duties under general direction, manages multiple projects concurrently with budgets that range in values per project and concurrently manages small scale designs, problem solving analyses and reports. Responsible for reviews of all projects managed by the office for adequacy of all aspects of complete design; code compliance and GU standards. The incumbent must coordinate all project design issues with Georgetown clients as well as appropriate staff counterparts in the other Planning and Facilities Management areas, the Department of Public Safety, the Office of University Information Services, representatives from Student Affairs and Residential Living, and other departments as applicable.

The incumbent manages multiple project teams; each consisting of from five to twenty team members. Incumbent must hold consultant and contractor team members accountable for performance of work stipulated by the contract scope of work and schedule.

title: Technical Program Lead
description:
The Undersea Systems Division at Leidos currently has an opening for a Technical Program Lead to support a customer site in San Diego, California. This is an exciting opportunity to apply systems engineering, naval operations, test and evaluation, and technical project-management experience in support of large-scale fleet activities and critical maritime missions.


The selected candidate will serve as the onsite Technical Program Led and senior technical representative, working closely with the Leidos Project Manager, customer leadership, engineers, fleet personnel, operational stakeholders, and government representatives. The position will support day-to-day onsite execution of program activities while also contributing directly to systems engineering, integration, test, and evaluation efforts.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the onsite senior technical representative for Leidos at the customer site in San Diego.
  • Work side by side with customer leadership and technical personnel to support day-to-day program execution and mission priorities.
  • Support the Leidos Project Manager with program planning, execution, customer coordination, schedule management, risk management, and delivery of program commitments.
  • Lead and coordinate engineering activities across multiple technical disciplines and stakeholder organizations.
  • Translate customer operational needs into technically sound engineering approaches, priorities, requirements, and recommendations.
  • Coordinate with engineers, subcontractors, fleet personnel, operators, government stakeholders, and program leadership to resolve technical and operational issues.
  • Track technical scope, milestones, schedules, deliverables, action items, risks, issues, dependencies, and decisions.
  • Maintain project-management artifacts, including project plans, schedules, milestone trackers, risk and issue registers, action-item logs, and status reports.

  • Review engineering products and ensure technical deliverables are accurate, complete, consistent, and aligned with customer and program requirements.

  • Support test and evaluation planning, assessment, and reporting activities as needed; extensive at-sea testing is not expected to be the primary responsibility.
  • Prepare and deliver technical briefings, program-status updates, decision presentations, risk updates, and recommendations to senior military and government leadership.
  • Analyze technical and operational information to identify deficiencies, risks, limitations, dependencies, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Coordinate responses to customer requests and ensure follow-up actions are completed on schedule.

  • Experience working directly with customer, government, military, engineering, or operational stakeholders to address technical requirements and mission needs.
  • Experience leading or coordinating engineering activities across multiple technical disciplines or organizations.
  • Experience supporting program execution, including schedule management, deliverables, action items, risks, issues, stakeholder coordination, and status reporting.
  • Experience developing, reviewing, or managing technical documentation, engineering analyses, requirements, system designs, integration products, or program deliverables.
  • Experience analyzing technical or operational information and communicating recommendations through written products, briefings, status reports, and presentations.
  • Experience facilitating technical meetings, program reviews, working groups, or customer engagements.
  • Ability to work effectively in a customer-facing environment alongside senior government, military, engineering, and program personnel.
  • Ability to balance systems engineering responsibilities with onsite Deputy Project Manager duties.
  • Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally, including overseas travel several times per year.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience serving as a Deputy Project Manager, Assistant Project Manager, technical lead, chief engineer, or equivalent onsite program representative.
  • Experience coordinating across government organizations, engineering teams, fleet personnel, contractors, operational commands, and other stakeholders.
  • Experience with software development, scripting, or software-intensive systems.

title: Senior Security Engineer
description:

As a Senior Security Engineer, you'll play a key role in helping protect Beca's information assets and technology platforms while supporting our ongoing digital transformation journey. Working within our Technology team, you'll partner closely with architects, engineers and platform owners to embed security best practice across enterprise systems, cloud environments, applications, data platforms and emerging AI-enabled technologies.


This is a highly collaborative role where you'll provide specialist guidance, influence security outcomes, and help teams make informed decisions that balance risk, security and business needs. You'll contribute to security architecture reviews, threat modelling, security assurance activities, incident response, and the development of security standards, patterns and controls that can be consistently applied across the organisation.


Working in a predominantly Microsoft technology environment, you'll have the opportunity to shape security practices across a large and complex organisation while staying at the forefront of evolving technologies, cyber threats and security frameworks. Depending on your background, you may also contribute to strengthening Beca's emerging AI security and governance capabilities as we continue to modernise and innovate.

  • Significant experience in security engineering, cybersecurity, cloud security or infrastructure security within medium to large-scale environments.
  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft security technologies and modern security practices across cloud, applications, platforms and infrastructure.
  • Experience conducting threat modelling, risk assessments, security reviews and implementing effective security controls.
  • Knowledge of recognised security and governance frameworks such as ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework and related industry standards.

title: Field Applications Specialist - West Region
description:
As a result of the combination of the BD Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions business with Waters Corporation (NYSE: WAT), by applying to this role, you will be applying for a position with Waters. Waters is a global leader in life sciences, dedicated to accelerating the benefits of pioneering science through analytical technologies, informatics, and service. With a focus on regulated, high-volume testing environments, Waters’ innovative portfolio harnesses deep scientific expertise across biology, chemistry, and physics. Waters collaborates with analytical laboratories around the world to advance the release of effective, high-quality medicines, assure the safety of food and water, and drive better patient outcomes by detecting diseases earlier, managing routine infections, and combatting growing antibiotic resistance. Through a shared culture of relentless innovation, Waters’ passionate team of approximately 16,000 colleagues partner with customers to turn scientific challenges into breakthroughs that improve lives worldwide.



We are the people who give possibilities purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.





Job Description

Location: Field-Based – West Region


Reporting To: Field Applications Specialist Manager, U.S. Region

Position Summary

Enable science. Drive adoption. Deliver customer outcomes.

At Waters, Field Applications Specialists are critical to ensuring customers realize the full value of their investment through expert scientific engagement, application guidance, and workflow optimization. Operating at the intersection of science and customer success, you guide users from onboarding through long-term adoption—translating complex technologies into meaningful scientific and operational outcomes.

This role goes beyond troubleshooting. It requires the ability to understand customer workflows, deliver impactful training, and proactively drive utilization and adoption. You will partner closely with commercial, service, and marketing teams to strengthen customer outcomes, increase product adoption, and uncover opportunities for growth.

This is a high-impact role where scientific expertise, customer engagement, and execution directly influence utilization, customer retention, and long-term value creation.

Role Purpose

As part of the Waters Biosciences division, ensure successful customer onboarding, product adoption, and sustained success by providing high-impact technical training, workflow optimization, and application expertise that enables customers to achieve their desired outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Customer Engagement & Training

  • Lead customer onboarding to ensure a seamless transition from purchase to implementation

  • Deliver high-quality, application-focused training tailored to customer workflows and expertise levels

  • Educate customers on best practices to maximize instrument and application performance

  • Support initial setup, validation, and readiness of customer workflows

  • Reinforce value realization and ensure achievement of intended outcomes

  • Build strong, trusted relationships with scientific stakeholders

  • Support broader customer success initiatives aligned to business objectives

Expansion & Opportunity Identification

  • Identify opportunities to expand application usage and workflow breadth

  • Surface unmet needs for additional products, reagents, or capabilities

  • Partner with Account Managers and Technical Sales Specialists to support growth opportunities

  • Contribute insights to territory and account development strategies

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with commercial, technical sales, service, and marketing teams

  • Support coordinated, account-based customer engagement strategies

  • Provide field insights to inform product development and training programs

  • Contribute to a collaborative, team-based customer success model

What Success Looks Like

  • Enables customers to achieve meaningful scientific and operational outcomes

  • Accelerates onboarding and reduces time to productivity

  • Minimizes technical barriers and improves implementation success

  • Increases product utilization and application adoption

  • Improves customer satisfaction, retention, and loyalty

  • Identifies and supports account expansion opportunities

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or related field

  • Hands-on experience with flow cytometry applications and cell sorting

  • Strong troubleshooting capabilities across complex workflows

  • Ability to translate scientific concepts into practical application

  • Strong training, communication, and presentation skills

  • Valid driver’s license with at least 3 years of driving history

  • Ability and willingness to travel extensively (60–70%), including multi-day overnight travel

Preferred

  • Advanced degree in life sciences or related field

  • Experience with spectral flow cytometry

  • Experience operating and troubleshooting cell sorters

  • Prior customer-facing application support or training experience

  • Familiarity with FlowJo, Infinicyt, OMIQ, or FCS Express

  • Experience in workflow optimization and method development

  • Experience working cross-functionally in commercial or field environments

Work Environment & Travel

  • Field-based role with frequent on-site and remote customer engagement

  • Travel driven by customer and business needs

Why Waters

Waters plays a critical role in advancing scientific discovery and improving human health. Our teams partner with leading organizations across Pharma, Biotech, Academic, and Government sectors to solve complex scientific challenges.

As part of Waters, you will:

  • Enable customers to achieve meaningful scientific outcomes

  • Work with innovative technologies and applications

  • Collaborate across scientific and commercial teams

  • Directly contribute to customer success and long-term value creation

Who Thrives in This Role

  • Scientists passionate about training, teaching, and enabling others

  • Customer-centric professionals who build long-term scientific partnerships

  • Problem-solvers who enjoy optimizing workflows and applications

  • Collaborative partners who work effectively across teams

  • Self-driven individuals committed to delivering high-impact field engagement

Who This Role Is Not For

  • Individuals seeking non-customer-facing or purely transactional roles

  • Those uncomfortable with travel and field-based engagement

  • Candidates who prefer reactive rather than proactive customer interaction

Equal Opportunity

Waters is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to building an inclusive workplace where all employees can thrive.

At BD, we prioritize on-site collaboration because we believe it fosters creativity, innovation, and effective problem-solving, which are essential in the fast-paced healthcare industry. For most roles, we require a minimum of 4 days of in-office presence per week to maintain our culture of excellence and ensure smooth operations, while also recognizing the importance of flexibility and work-life balance. Compensation

The expected Base Pay Range for this role is $95,600 - $153,000 USD Annually plus incentives. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and geographic location.

Why Join Us?

To find purpose in the possibilities, we need people who can see the bigger picture, who understand the human story that underpins everything we do. We welcome people with the imagination and drive to help us reinvent the future of healthcare. At BD, you’ll discover a culture in which you can learn, grow and thrive.

We believe that when people connect in person, we learn faster, collaborate more deeply, and build a stronger culture. Join us and enjoy a culture where face-to-face collaboration supports your learning, your progress, and your success.

title: Clinical Placement Coordinator
description:
About the Work Unit

The Office of Clinical Placement collaborates with faculty, program directors, students, and clinical partners to facilitate productive clinical experiences. The office recruits and maintains clinical sites in Middle Tennessee and coordinates agreements and agency requirements for distance students across the United States and, when needed, internationally.

Key Functions and Expected Performance

  • Coordinate clinical placements for assigned academic programs, ensuring timely and appropriate clinical experiences.
  • Manage clinical placement operations to support local and distance students.
  • Provide strategic oversight of clinical placement processes to ensure compliance with licensure, regulatory, and Board of Nursing requirements.
  • Oversee accuracy, integrity, and optimization of clinical placement data within the Exxat system
  • Lead clinical site recruitment and geographic expansion efforts through targeted outreach and relationship-building
  • Ensure consistent, high quality placement experiences through process improvement and operational oversight.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with clinical sites, healthcare organizations, preceptors, faculty, students, and program leadership.
  • Recruit and develop clinical partnerships to meet program needs and support geographic expansion.
  • Coordinate student placement assignments, schedules, requirements, and changes.
  • Monitor student compliance with immunizations, certifications, background checks, drug screenings, health requirements, and site-specific requirements.
  • Manage clinical site records, affiliation agreements, placement documentation, and compliance data.
  • Ensure placements align with curriculum, accreditation standards, regulatory requirements, and clinical site expectations.
  • Monitor deadlines and proactively address placement gaps, changes, cancellations, and other challenges.
  • Serve as a primary resource for student and stakeholder questions and resolve complex placement concerns.
  • Collaborate with faculty and program leadership to align placement strategies with academic and program needs.
  • Maintain accurate placement data using Exxat and other databases and administrative systems.
  • Participate in meetings, training, professional development, and special projects as assigned.

  • Maintain confidentiality and comply with institutional policies and applicable regulations

Supervisory Relationships

This position does not have supervisory responsibility. It reports administratively and functionally to the Director of Clinical Affairs Operations.

Education and Certifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • Experience in healthcare, higher education, clinical education, student services, program coordination, or a related field preferred.
  • Strong organizational, project management, problem-solving, and time-management skills.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with clinical placement management systems such as Exxat preferred.

Key Characteristics for Success

  • Adaptability: Effectively responds to changing site availability, student needs, schedules, and program requirements.
  • Professionalism: Demonstrates sound judgment, accountability, discretion, and respect in all interactions.

  • Proactive: Anticipates needs, identifies opportunities, and takes action without waiting to be directed.

  • Takes Initiative: Comfortable identifying what needs to be done and moving work forward independently.

  • Ownership Mindset: Takes responsibility for outcomes, follows through on commitments, and sees projects through to completion.

  • Highly Autonomous: Works effectively with minimal supervision, using sound judgment to prioritize and make decisions.

  • Resourceful: Finds solutions, overcomes obstacles, and knows when and how to seek support when needed.

  • Accountable: Takes responsibility for both successes and challenges, learns from outcomes, and continuously improves.

  • Self-Directed: Effectively manages priorities, time, and workload while maintaining high standards of quality.

  • Action-Oriented: Moves from ideas to execution quickly and maintains momentum without requiring constant direction.

  • Organization & Planning: Effectively manages multiple placements, sites, deadlines, and competing priorities.
  • Communication: Communicates clearly and professionally with diverse stakeholders.
  • Relationship Management: Builds collaborative, long-term partnerships with clinical and academic partners.
  • Problem Solving: Anticipates challenges and develops practical solutions.
  • Attention to Detail: Maintains accurate placement, compliance, and affiliation records.
  • Student Service: Provides responsive, professional, and student-focused support.

title: Associate, Global Private Wealth - Investor Relations
description:

For over forty years, HarbourVest has been home to a committed team of professionals with an entrepreneurial spirit and a desire to deliver impactful solutions to our clients and investing partners.   • Strong work ethic; genuine passion for excellence and constant improvement.

Education Preferred:

  • Master’s degree is a bonus.
  • CFA or CAIA is a plus

Experience:

  • Min 3 years of experience in asset management and/or private markets distribution fundraising or product specialist roles, primarily targeting the wholesale and wealth client segments.

title: Senior Rotating Equipment Specialist
description:
Job Summary

At PEMEX Deer Park, the role of the Senior Rotating Equipment Specialist is to provide technical support to Production and Maintenance sitewide for ~60 Critical Machinery Assets. The role will provide technical and field support for planned and unplanned machinery outages, support turnarounds, and manage critical spare parts. To accomplish this, the role is empowered to be the owner of Technical Assurance for all Critical machines and the supporting auxiliary equipment.



Accountabilities & Responsibilities:

Technical Competence: Key areas for operational equipment competency include:

  • Rotating Equipment: General Purpose Pumps, Electric Motors, General Purpose Turbines, Shaft Sealing Systems, Lubrication Systems, Fin Fans, and Blowers.
  • Special Purpose Rotating Equipment: Operation and Repair of Centrifugal Compressors, Multi-Stage Steam Turbines, Turbo Generators, Gearboxes, Reciprocating Compressors, Dry Gas Seals and Oil Seals, High Energy Pumps, Skill level knowledge of API 686 and API 687.

Delivery: Build strong working relationships with and leverage support from a broad range of stakeholders and peers, including:

  • Production Teams – Asset Managers (PUMs), Productions Specialists, Operators, Maintenance Supervisor, Inspectors, Process Engineers, and Safety Representative
  • Central Engineering – Rotating and Static Equipment subject matter experts, other engineering counterparts in Electrical, Civil, Control Systems and Environmental Engineering.
  • Maintenance and Turnarounds – Planners, Execution Team Leads, Field Coordinators, and Cost Controllers
  • Project Engineering
  • Support Functions – Contracts & Procurement, Warehouse, SAP and IMS Superusers, Emergency Response
  • Third Parties – Vendors, Fabrication/Repair Shops, and Engineering Contractors

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

The Senior Rotating Equipment is the first point of contact for anything related to the operation and maintenance of Critical Machinery.

Operations Support

  • Work with Operations and Maintenance counterparts to solve day-to-day problems, ensuring safe and reliable unit operation.
  • Participate in quarterly production team meetings to maintain awareness of key activities and unit operating status.
  • Conduct routine field walkthroughs with operations, maintenance, and inspection to proactively evaluate concerns with equipment and provide recommendations.
  • Support as a key contributor during stabilization and recovery from operational upsets.
  • Escalate troubleshooting to the Senior Rotating Equipment Engineer when necessary.

Technical Assurance

  • Develop Quality Plans for execution of maintenance on Critical Rotating Equipment.
  • Support work scope development and field execution for Critical Rotating Equipment
  • Coordinate mechanical equipment surveillance during routine and non-routine operation.
  • Participate in production unit pre-startup safety reviews and commissioning activities for MOC or after Turnaround.
  • Support Overhaul activities in outside shops.
  • Review teardown reports and provide recommendations for critical equipment repair.
  • Review equipment BOM and ensure its accuracy prior to maintenance events.
  • Primary owner for critical spare parts including condition, storage, and preservation.
  • Perform annual audits on critical spares to ensure compliance.
  • Contribute to MEDR and maintain Equipment Condition History reports in IMS
  • Support RCM work Process for Critical Machinery.

Critical Work Processes

  • Manage Threats and Opportunities (MTO): Identify and prioritize threats and opportunities related to mechanical equipment, utilize problem solving skills to frame potential solutions, and take action to drive resolution.
  • Management of Change (MOC): Develop technical design bases, provide and facilitate technical assurance and hazard screening of design, assist with maintenance planning and execution activities, lead pre-startup safety reviews, and verify change close-out activities.
  • Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM): Manage and continuously improve asset care strategies for both fixed and rotating equipment using consistent methodologies and a standardized approach.
  • Maintenance Execution (ME): Drive compliance for critical planned maintenance, review deferral justifications, and seek optimization opportunities.
  • Process Safety Compliance: Manage and timely implement Process Safety recommendations for the assigned production areas.
  • Causal Learning: Participate in and occasionally lead Causal Learning investigations to support continuous improvement.


KEY CHALLENGES

  • Able to leverage technical and interpersonal skills to drive work items.
  • Able to prioritize a high workload within the engineering team.
  • Able to work independently with minimal supervision while completing work deliverables with a high level of detail and quality.
  • Able to work at all levels of the organization and have the appropriate skills to influence others in the organization.


ROLE REQUIREMENTS

  • Must have legal authorization to work in the US on a full-time basis.
  • Minimum five (10) years of experience in a related manufacturing industry.
  • Proven experience with maintenance and reliability concepts, including a sound understanding of engineering and maintenance processes. Knowledge of the concepts of risk management, Reliability Centered Maintenance, Management of Change, and structured problem solving.
  • Excellent troubleshooting, analytical, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to interface with personnel from diverse backgrounds at all levels of the organization. Proven ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects.
  • Demonstrated skill in working with teams to achieve a common goal.



Qualifications:

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Prior experience in support of special purpose rotating equipment.
  • Prior experience with concepts related to maintenance and reliability, risk assessment, Management of Change, and structured problem solving.
  • Knowledge of industry codes and standards, and their application within the refining and petrochemical industries.
  • Prior experience with BOM and spare parts management including repair, inspection, and preservation.


Education, Experience and Skills

Education and Experience:

  • High School Diploma or GED
  • Prior direct full-time work experience in a refining or petrochemical manufacturing complex. Minimum of 10 years.

Physical requirements:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions:

  • Lifting requirements of 25 lbs.
  • Walking distances of up to a mile
  • Climbing portable and vessel ladders to elevations over 100 feet
  • 25-50% of work is performed in an outside petrochemical manufacturing environment.
  • Occasional extended work hours during planned and unplanned events.
  • Must currently hold or be able to qualify to receive a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) card. Note, information regarding TWIC qualification standards may be found at https://www.tsa.gov/forindustry/twic

title: Head of Fire, Health & Safety
description:
The Head of Fire, Health & Safety is responsible for ensuring a positive safety culture is embedded across Harrods, while ensuring legislative requirements are met and safety-related risks are effectively managed.


You will lead the strategic development and delivery of our Fire, Health & Safety strategy, policies, standards and operational plans, ensuring the highest levels of compliance across our estate. This includes our iconic Knightsbridge store, production kitchens, warehouses and distribution centre.


Working closely with the Director of Security, you will provide strategic leadership and expert advice across all aspects of fire, health and safety and risk management, with the safety of our colleagues and customers at the heart of everything you do.


You will also lead and develop a multi-disciplinary, experienced team across Health & Safety and Fire, creating a high-performing, engaged team focused on continuous improvement.


About the Role


As Head of Fire, Health & Safety, you will:


  • Develop and deliver the strategic vision for Fire, Health & Safety across the business and ensure it is embedded.
  • Act as the organisation's subject matter expert, providing senior-level advice and guidance on fire, health and safety, building safety and risk.
  • Ensure policies, procedures and operational standards remain compliant with legislation and recognised best practice.
  • Provide specialist advice on building projects and upgrades, including the review of plans and proposed works.
  • Oversee significant risk assessments, audits and assurance activities across the business.
  • Lead the investigation and analysis of serious incidents, ensuring lessons are identified and appropriate actions implemented.
  • Monitor fire safety compliance, including the adequacy and maintenance of firefighting equipment and associated controls.
  • Develop effective governance, reporting, KPIs and management information, presenting key risks and findings to senior leaders and external stakeholders where required.
  • Drive continuous improvement, proactively challenging the business and promoting a strong, positive safety culture.
  • Lead, coach and develop your team, setting clear expectations and creating an environment of high performance, engagement and accountability.
  • Deputise for the Director of Security when required, taking responsibility for strategic and operational decision-making in their absence.

About You


You will be an experienced Fire, Health & Safety leader with the credibility and expertise to operate effectively at a senior level within a complex, fast-paced organisation.


You will have:


  • A NEBOSH Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety, or equivalent Level 6 NVQ.
  • Chartered Membership of IOSH (CMIOSH), or be working towards this.
  • Extensive knowledge of Health & Safety, Fire Safety and Building Safety legislation and the ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical solutions.
  • Strong governance and assurance experience, including presenting risk and compliance information at executive level.
  • A track record of developing and delivering strategic Fire, Health & Safety plans, supported by clear KPIs and measurable outcomes.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to balance commercial priorities with regulatory compliance and best practice.
  • Strong risk management and decision-making capability, with a proactive and pragmatic approach.
  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the confidence to engage and challenge senior leaders, operational teams, regulators and external partners.
  • Proven senior leadership experience in leading, developing and motivating Health, Safety and Fire Safety professionals, fostering a high-performing culture focused on compliance, risk reduction and continuous improvement. A demonstrable passion for Health & Safety.

Working Pattern


This is a highly visible, operational leadership role and we prefer five days per week on site, with a minimum of four days on site. The role requires flexibility to work across our sites.


The working pattern will include approximately one weekend in every six, with two days off in lieu during the week. Bank and Public Holidays are considered normal working days, and occasional additional or changed hours may be required to meet the needs of the business.


Uniquely You


At Harrods, we believe anything is possible. We celebrate and welcome applications from all cultures, backgrounds, tastes and experiences, and we're proud to create an environment where people from all walks of life can grow and thrive. What makes you unique makes us exceptional.


If you want to know more about life at Harrods, search #TogetherHarrods on LinkedIn, or follow us on Instagram @togetherharrods.

title: Dynamics 365/Power Platform Developer
description:
Dynamics 365/Power Platform Developer

Microsoft Dynamics 365 • Power Platform • Configuration & Development • Tier III Support

Location: Remote / Contractor Site, with occasional in-person meetings or workshops as required

Clearance: Must be a US Citizen, Ability to obtain a DHS clearance required; current DHS clearance preferred.

Work Status: Remote

A Role with Purpose and Impact

Dev Technology is supporting the operations, maintenance, and continued enhancement of a mission-essential platform in an environment built primarily on Microsoft Dynamics 365, SharePoint, Microsoft 365, Power Platform Government, and Azure.

In this role, you will help configure, extend, troubleshoot, and improve Dynamics 365 and Power Platform capabilities that support case and matter management, reporting, dashboards, approval processes, knowledge management, and day-to-day user needs. You will partner closely with the client development and maintenance teams as well as the inhouse Helpdesk and Government users.

This role is designed for a hands-on Microsoft platform specialist who can move comfortably between configuration, development, troubleshooting, customer support, and release planning in a secure federal environment.

Dynamics 365 Delivery and User Support

This role blends Dynamics 365/Power Platform development with configuration and advanced user support. You will:

  • Configure and extend Dynamics 365 Online and Power Platform capabilities to meet evolving business requirements.
  • Develop and maintain reports, Advanced Find views, queries, dashboards, approval processes, and knowledge base/customer service portal capabilities.
  • Configure Dynamics CRM organizations and support release management, deployment, and troubleshooting for release-ready solutions.
  • Work directly with the client’s Tasking System users to provide technical assistance, configuration support, training, and solutions that may not require a formal release.
  • Partner with development and maintenance teams to identify recurring needs, inform future release features, and translate user issues into practical configuration or development changes.
  • Apply a user-first approach and sound UI/UX practices when developing or modifying user-facing capabilities, with a focus on usability, consistency, and user adoption.

You will remain close to both the platform and its users—troubleshooting issues, validating changes, supporting testing, maintaining documentation, and helping ensure Dynamics 365 capabilities remain secure, supportable, and aligned with the agency standards.

Who Thrives Here

People who thrive in this role bring strong Microsoft-platform expertise and a practical, customer-focused approach to delivery. They:

  • Enjoy solving business problems through a mix of configuration and code rather than defaulting to custom development.
  • Can explain Dynamics 365 and Power Platform capabilities clearly to technical and non-technical users.
  • Are comfortable investigating production issues, tracing root causes, and working across application, identity, integration, and data dependencies.
  • Value secure configuration, disciplined release practices, documentation, and repeatable support processes.
  • Can shift between planned enhancement work and responsive Tier III customer support.
  • Collaborate well with developers, helpdesk staff, Government stakeholders, and other Microsoft platform teams.

The Opportunity

title: Solar Array Engineer, Mechanical
description:
Vast is developing next-generation space stations and space infrastructure using an incremental, hardware-rich, and low-cost approach. Vast is rapidly developing its multi-module Haven Station to ensure a continuous human presence in space for America and its allies, enabling advanced microgravity research and manufacturing, and unlocking a new space economy for government, corporate, and private customers. Haven Demo’s 2025 success made Vast the only operational commercial space station company to fly and operate its own spacecraft. Next, Haven-1 is expected to become the world’s first commercial space station when it launches in 2027, followed by additional Haven modules. Additionally, the company recently announced Vast Satellite, a high-power satellite product line leveraging its space station components and the heritage of Haven Demo.

Headquartered in Long Beach, California, and with more than 1,000 employees and over a billion dollars in private capital, Vast has built the facilities required to manufacture and operate America’s next space station. The company plans to develop future habitats and systems for the Moon and Mars, dedicated space stations for government partners, and other crewed systems that will unlock the expanding long-term space economy.

Vast is looking for a Solar Array Engineer, Mechanical, reporting to the Principal Power Systems Engineer, to support the design, analysis, build, and test of mechanisms for solar array deployment and articulation on human-rated space stations.

This will be a full-time, exempt position located in our Long Beach location.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and analyze mechanisms for solar array deployment, including spring-driven hinges, latches, dampers, and hold-down/release devices
  • Design and analyze mechanisms for solar array articulation, including motorized gimbals, gear trains, bearings, and drive electronics interfaces
  • Build and maintain torque budgets for deployment and articulation mechanisms, including friction, harness resistance, disturbance torques, and margin verification per NASA-STD-5017B
  • Select and specify bearings, lubricants, motors, gearboxes, encoders/resolvers, and other drivetrain components for the space environment
  • Perform or support mechanism life analysis — bearing life, lubricant life, wear analysis — and define qualification test programs to demonstrate life margin
  • Design for integration and test — develop deployment test procedures, gravity offload approaches, and workmanship screens
  • Interface with structures, thermal, GN&C, and power teams to ensure mechanisms meet system-level requirements (deployed stiffness, pointing accuracy, disturbance torques, power transfer across rotating joints)
  • Support environmental test campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, shock, life testing) per SMC-S-016
  • Perform or support failure analysis, root cause investigation, and mechanism anomaly resolution
  • Participate in design reviews, FMEA/FMECA, and technical documentation for internal and NASA deliverables

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or related discipline
  • 5–10 years of experience designing, building, and testing electromechanical systems — preferably mechanisms for spacecraft, satellites, or robotic systems
  • Demonstrated experience with mechanism design fundamentals: bearings, gears, motors, springs, fasteners, and structural load paths
  • Ability to build and defend a torque budget or force budget for a mechanism from first principles
  • Experience with environmental testing of mechanical hardware (vibration, thermal cycling, life testing)
  • Hands-on experience — you have built, assembled, or integrated the hardware you designed

Preferred Skills & Experience:

  • Experience with spring-driven deployable mechanisms — hinges, latches, dampers, hold-down/release devices. Understanding of deployment torque margin verification and ground test challenges (gravity offload, thermal effects on torque budget)
  • Experience with motorized mechanisms — gimbals, solar array drive assemblies (SADAs), antenna positioners, or robotic actuators. Familiarity with BLDC motors, stepper motors, gearbox types (planetary, harmonic drive, cycloidal), and anti-backlash techniques
  • Knowledge of tribology for the space environment — solid film lubricants (MoS₂, WS₂), space-rated greases (Braycote, Pennzane), lubricant life analysis, and the challenges of ground testing vs. on-orbit performance
  • Familiarity with NASA-STD-5017B (mechanism design and analysis) including torque margin requirements and life testing philosophy
  • Experience with bearing design for space mechanisms — angular contact bearing configurations, preload methods, thermal effects on preload, and lubrication-limited life analysis
  • Understanding of control and feedback architecture for pointing mechanisms — encoders, resolvers, motor-side vs. load-side feedback, backlash compensation
  • Familiarity with FBD construction and deployment dynamics — conservation of angular momentum, spacecraft disturbance torques during deployment, and ACS interaction
  • Familiarity with SMC-S-016 or GEVS environmental test requirements
  • CAD experience in NX or similar (Teamcenter experience is a plus)
  • Experience with analysis tools — hand calculations, MATLAB/Python for mechanism dynamics, FEA for structural assessment of mechanism components

Additional Requirements:

  • Ability to travel up to 50% of the time
  • Willingness to work evenings and/or weekends to support critical mission milestones
  • Ability to lift up to 25lbs unassisted
  • Specific certifications, as appropriate
Pay Range: California
$112,340—$230,472 USD

We calibrate level and compensation to the selected candidate's experience and demonstrated capability. We welcome applicants across a range of experience levels to apply.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Base salary will vary depending on job-related knowledge, education, skills, experience, business needs, and market demand. Salary is just one component of our comprehensive compensation package. Full-time employees also receive company equity, as well as access to a full suite of compelling benefits and perks, including: medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents, generous paid time off; up to 20+ days of vacation for exempt staff and up to 10+ days of vacation for non-exempt staff with the ability to cash-out unused vacation annually, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, ClassPass credits, personalized mental healthcare through Spring Health, and other discounts and perks. We also take pride in offering exceptional food perks, with snacks, drip coffee & onsite barista, cold drinks, and dinner meals remaining free of charge, and lunch subsidized as part of Vast’s ongoing commitment to providing high-quality meals for employees.
