title: Data Scientist
description:
Leidos is seeking a Senior Data Scientist to support an upcoming program in Chantilly, VA. This role will provide senior-level expertise in the design, development, integration, and analysis of complex data environments. The successful candidate will develop methods, processes, and systems to consolidate, transform, manage, and analyze structured and unstructured data from diverse and disparate sources.

The Senior Data Scientist will work across applications and data environments to identify analytical data requirements, improve data quality and accessibility, develop analytical solutions, and enable the effective use of data for operational and mission needs. The role requires the ability to understand complex data flows and systems, identify issues and dependencies, and translate technical data challenges into actionable solutions for both technical teams and leadership.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and implement methods and processes to collect, integrate, transform, manage, and analyze large and complex datasets from disparate sources.
  • Develop and apply advanced statistical concepts, algorithms, queries, and automated processes to clean, model, integrate, and evaluate structured and unstructured data.
  • Analyze complex data flows between applications and identify opportunities to improve data quality, integrity, accessibility, and usability.
  • Identify analytical data requirements and develop solutions to support operational, business, and mission objectives.
  • Evaluate data structures, sources, interfaces, and dependencies to identify gaps, inconsistencies, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Collaborate with software engineers, data engineers, system administrators, analysts, and other technical stakeholders to integrate and leverage data across applications and environments.
  • Support the development and integration of ML/AI capabilities by understanding data requirements, data preparation, and the use of data throughout the ML/AI lifecycle.
  • Develop and maintain automated data processes and support data integration within CI/CD environments.
  • Investigate complex data and system issues, determine root causes, and develop practical solutions.
  • Communicate technical findings, data issues, risks, and recommended solutions clearly to technical teams and program leadership.
  • Contribute to data standards, governance, documentation, and dataset management processes.

Basic Qualifications

  • Requires a bachelor’s degree and 12+ years of relevant experience, or Masters degree with 10+ years of experience. Additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
  • 6+ years of experience managing, integrating, or troubleshooting data flows between applications and/or systems.
  • Strong understanding of how application data is generated, managed, transformed, transferred, and consumed across interconnected systems.
  • Demonstrated experience analyzing complex technical problems and developing practical, data-driven solutions.
  • Experience identifying analytical data requirements and determining appropriate data sources, structures, and processes to support those requirements.
  • Experience with dataset management, data quality, data integration, and associated processes.
  • Understanding of software development and CI/CD pipelines and how data processes integrate with application development and deployment environments.
  • Understanding of how machine learning and artificial intelligence capabilities utilize, process, and derive value from data.

Clearance

  • Active TS/SCI clearance with Polygraph is required to be considered for this position.
  • US Citizenship is required

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ServiceNow, particularly ITSM and CMDB.
  • Experience with Splunk or other enterprise data/logging platforms.
  • Experience with Cameo or other systems engineering/model-based systems engineering (MBSE) tools.
  • Experience developing reports, dashboards, data visualizations, or other analytical products for leadership and operational stakeholders.
  • Experience with data engineering, ETL/ELT processes, APIs, data pipelines, or application-to-application data integration.
  • Experience working with cloud, distributed, or enterprise-scale data environments.
  • Experience supporting data analytics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, or other advanced data-driven capabilities.
  • Experience documenting data architectures, data flows, interfaces, and system dependencies.

title: Field Credit Officer (Ebonyi)
description:
About Us:

Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere.

Job Title: Field Credit Officer

Reports to: Regional Credit Manager

Employment Type: Outsourced

Work Mode: Onsite

About this role:

As a Field Credit Officer, you would be saddled with the duty of onboarding and managing businesses that would access our credit products. You would be tasked with growing your loan portfolio while maintaining profitability by ensuring that all loans are repaid as and when due. As a result, you would play a vital role in the assessment of these businesses during their credit application and leverage innovative tools we have developed to help you monitor their performance during the course of the loan.

You would also be responsible for making deductions from several information sources about the 5Cs of credit, with capacity, character, and capital as major priorities. Make recommendations to management before, during, and after the disbursement of a loan facility as to the best actions to be taken, considering several economic factors.

Responsibilities:

  • Identify and onboard viable businesses within your assigned geographical area to open business accounts with Moniepoint
  • Engage customers to ensure optimal usage of accounts to allow them to qualify for access to credit
  • Review and approve (or decline) loan requests by thoroughly analyzing all the data available
  • Embark on physical visitation to potential borrowers’ business places for evaluation of business books, taking inventory and turnover into consideration
  • Meet gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets by maintaining a healthy number of loan customers while ensuring that all loans in portfolio are performing
  • Monitor active loan portfolio to ensure continued use of business account and loan repayment performance
  • Perform all other credit-related functions as may be assigned by a supervisor

Experience & Background:

  • Minimum of an OND in any business-related discipline
  • Minimum of 2 years’ experience in a sales role for credit products in a financial institution
  • Demonstrable knowledge of credit risk analysis
  • Good knowledge of financial analysis is an added advantage

Skills & Competencies:

  • Apt attention to details
  • Proven simple/complex analytical skills
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Agility and perseverance

What success looks like in this role:

  • Consistent achievement of gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets.
  • Maintaining a healthy, performing loan portfolio with minimized default rates through rigorous physical visitations and monitoring.
  • Successful onboarding and engagement of viable businesses that actively utilize Moniepoint business accounts.
  • Accurate credit risk assessments based on key factors like capacity, character, and capital.

Why join us:

  • Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.
  • Opportunity to work with Africa’s fastest-growing fintech and make a direct impact on business growth across the region.

title: Director of Programs
description:
The Opportunity:

As the Director of Programs in Kanawha County, West Virginia, you will lead the launch and implementation of career readiness and life skills programming through the Skilled West Virginia workforce ecosystem. Reporting to the EVP, Strategy & Growth, your role is vital in designing, managing, and delivering career training and wraparound support in a region that values relationships, trust, resilience, and second chances.

You will serve as the primary point of contact for participants, partners, and community stakeholders — coaching individuals to overcome barriers, facilitating career readiness workshops, and aligning local resources (training providers, recovery services, and employers) for program success. Your ability to mentor, lead initiatives, and foster strong community connections across Kanawha County and the surrounding southern coalfield counties will be critical to both short-term participant success and long-term workforce development in the region.

This role also includes temporary responsibilities in program design and implementation, ensuring a smooth program launch and participant progression. Once the program is established, your work will focus entirely on participant engagement, success coaching, recovery-informed support, and workforce placement.


Organization Overview:

As part of Skilled US’s commitment to empowering adults in marginalized and underserved communities, the Director of Programs plays a crucial role in supporting individuals through career transitions and growing our footprint in West Virginia. Skilled West Virginia is the West Virginia operating unit of Skilled US, whose mission is to provide the tools, training, and resources necessary for individuals to secure high-demand jobs and achieve economic stability. Through comprehensive vocational programs, wraparound services, career counseling, networking, and mentorship — and, in West Virginia, integrated peer recovery support — we equip our participants with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in today’s job market. The success of our program graduates underscores the transformative impact of Skilled US in breaking the cycle of poverty and fostering long-term economic growth

Key Responsibilities:

Program Development & Implementation

  • Lead the design, facilitation, and launch of a local career readiness program tailored to the unique needs of Kanawha County and the surrounding southern West Virginia communities, including the recovery and dislocated-worker populations.
  • Collaborate with the EVP, Strategy & Growth to set program goals, timelines, and success indicators.
  • Coordinate with local organizations and training partners — including local community colleges and training programs, workforce-focused organizations, recovery service providers, and area employers — to ensure timely and smooth program delivery.
  • Track implementation milestones and make adjustments to improve quality and impact.
  • Hire, coach and manage a team in WV as funding becomes available.

Participant Success & Career Readiness Coaching

  • Serve as a trusted mentor and coach for participants, offering personalized guidance through enrollment, training, and job placement.
  • Create and facilitate in-person or virtual career and life skills workshops focused on communication, financial literacy, time management, and workplace expectations.
  • Identify barriers to success (e.g., transportation, housing, childcare, trauma, recovery maintenance, motivation) and help participants access needed supports, coordinating closely with embedded peer recovery support where applicable.
  • Monitor enrollment, withdrawals, and attendance to ensure consistent engagement and program completion.
  • Utilize motivational interviewing and trauma-informed techniques to help participants explore goals, strengthen intrinsic motivation, and resolve ambivalence about personal or professional growth.

Community & Partner Engagement

  • Build and sustain relationships with local employers, community leaders, training partners, recovery providers, and service agencies across Kanawha County and the southern coalfield region.
  • Organize work-based learning opportunities and employer site visits — including with Recovery-Ready Workplace employer partners — to connect participants with real-world experiences.
  • Promote Skilled US’s and Skilled West Virginia’s mission through community outreach, speaking engagements, and collaborative efforts.

Data & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date participant records using enrollment and CRM systems like Salesforce or HubSpot.
  • Collect and analyze participant progress data to inform decision-making and continuous improvement.
  • Prepare timely reports for leadership and funders — including grant and SNAP E&T compliance reporting — highlighting participant success stories and program outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications:
Education
  • Bachelor’s degree in social work, higher education, or a related field, or at least five years of relevant experience.

Work Experience

  • 5+ years working in adult education, career services, or workforce development.
  • Demonstrated success advising adult learners, managing career pathways, or building employer relationships.
  • Experience designing and implementing training programs, particularly in small, rural, or Appalachian communities.
  • Experience working with individuals in recovery, reentry, or other populations facing significant barriers is strongly preferred.

Skills & Knowledge

  • Proficiency in Excel, CRMs (Salesforce or similar), and data entry/reporting.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills, including the ability to lead workshops.
  • Deep understanding of case management, social emotional learning techniques, trauma-informed care, and career counseling.
  • Knowledge of funding sources and support systems such as SNAP E&T, WIOA, Workforce Pell, and recovery/reentry programs.
  • Familiarity with substance use disorder recovery principles and recovery-to-work models is a plus.

title: Investigative Data Analyst
description:
Leidos is seeking a Investigative Data Analyst to support data-driven decision-making by collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting complex information to identify trends, risks, vulnerabilities, and operational insights. This role combines advanced analytical skills, investigative research, quality assurance auditing, and executive-level communication to support organizational leadership. The ideal candidate is a self-motivated professional who excels in working with large datasets, developing meaningful visualizations, and translating technical findings into actionable recommendations.


*The Investigative Data Analyst will be a hybrid role, 50% onsite in the Fort Worth, TX office and 50% remote. The candidate for this role must be within commutable distance to the office location.

*This position will start as a part-time role with expectation of moving to full time status in January of 2027.


Primary Responsibilities:

  • Analyze complex datasets to identify trends, gaps, anomalies, risks, and potential integrity concerns through statistical and analytical modeling techniques.
  • Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, charts, graphs, and other visual products using Microsoft Excel, Power BI, and other analytical tools to communicate findings effectively.
  • Conduct research using government databases, internal data systems, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) resources to support investigations, operational assessments, and strategic initiatives.
  • Prepare executive summaries, investigative reports, briefing materials, status reports, and presentations for senior leadership, including executive and Congressional stakeholders.
  • Perform quality assurance reviews and audits of work products, closed cases, management inquiries, and operational processes to ensure compliance with established policies and standards.
  • Identify emerging trends, systemic vulnerabilities, and operational risks by connecting information across multiple data sources and organizational functions.
  • Translate complex technical analyses into clear, concise, and actionable recommendations tailored to audiences ranging from technical staff to executive leadership.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, program managers, analysts, investigators, and organizational leadership to support strategic initiatives and operational objectives.
  • Independently manage assigned projects, establish priorities, monitor timelines, and deliver high-quality work with minimal supervision.
  • Exercise sound judgment when evaluating sensitive information, recognizing anomalies, and determining when issues require escalation to management.
  • Support continuous process improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance data quality, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency.
  • Ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and appropriate handling of sensitive or restricted information.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship required
  • Clearance: Secret clearance or ability to obtain one
  • Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Statistics, Criminal Justice, Public Administration, or a related field and 2 years of relevant experieince. Equivalent professional experience may be considered.
  • Experience analyzing large and complex datasets to identify trends, risks, gaps, and operational insights.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including pivot tables, advanced formulas, data modeling, and analytical functions.
  • Demonstrated expertise using Microsoft Power BI to create dashboards, visualizations, and interactive reports.
  • Experience working with databases, government information systems, or other enterprise data repositories.
  • Knowledge of open-source intelligence (OSINT) research methodologies and publicly available information sources.
  • Strong technical writing skills with the ability to produce executive summaries, investigative reports, briefing documents, and formal correspondence.
  • Experience conducting quality assurance reviews, compliance audits, or performance evaluations.
  • Exceptional analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities with strong pattern recognition skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Proven ability to collaborate effectively across multiple organizational levels and functional areas.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple assignments and meet deadlines while working independently.
  • Demonstrated professionalism, integrity, discretion, and sound judgment when handling sensitive information.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting federal government agencies or regulatory organizations.
  • Familiarity with aviation, transportation, law enforcement, inspections, investigations, or regulatory compliance programs.
  • Experience with SQL, Python, R, or other analytical programming languages.
  • Knowledge of data governance, data quality management, and business intelligence best practices.
  • Experience with automated reporting tools, workflow applications, or enterprise case management systems.
  • Experience preparing executive-level briefings for senior government officials.

title: Process Development Chemist / Engineer
description:
Job Summary

Are you passionate about transforming innovative chemistry into scalable industrial processes? Join our Process R&D team in Kantvik and play a key role in developing next-generation biomaterials, health products, and sustainable technologies through hands-on laboratory and pilot-scale experimentation!

In this role, you will play a key role in developing and scaling innovative processes for biomolecules, biomaterials, and health-related products within IFF's global Health & Biosciences organization. This is a highly hands-on position where you will spend a significant portion of your time designing, executing, and evaluating laboratory and pilot-scale experiments while collaborating with cross-functional teams across R&D and manufacturing. You will translate scientific concepts into robust, scalable industrial processes, supporting projects from early development through commercial implementation. The role offers opportunities to contribute to technology transfers, manufacturing support, and continuous improvement initiatives across our global production network. We are looking for a curious, practical problem-solver who thrives in the laboratory, enjoys working close to the technology, and is motivated by transforming ideas into real-world solutions. The role is based in Kantvik, Kirkkonummi, Finland (onsite role). Be part of a collaborative, innovative, and globally connected team where together we can achieve greatness and make a real impact!

Where You'll Make a Difference

  • Lead and execute process development projects from laboratory concept through pilot-scale implementation and reporting
  • Perform hands-on laboratory and pilot plant experiments to develop and optimize chemical and biobased processes
  • Design, analyze, and interpret experimental results to support scale-up and commercialization activities
  • Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary global project teams, manufacturing sites, and external partners
  • Plan and coordinate daily laboratory and pilot plant activities to ensure project objectives and timelines are achieved
  • Support technology transfers, manufacturing start-ups, process troubleshooting, and plant optimization projects in Finland and internationally
  • Produce pilot-scale samples for customer evaluations and internal development activities
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to laboratory and pilot plant personnel within project teams
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives while promoting a strong Environment, Health and Safety culture

What Makes You the Right Fit

  • M.Sc. or Ph.D. in Organic Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field with strong organic chemistry expertise
  • Several years of relevant industrial experience in process development, chemical manufacturing, bioprocessing, or pulp & paper industries
  • Strong expertise in organic chemistry, including synthesis, characterization, and functional modification of polymers and particulate materials
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and support colleagues in organic chemistry methodologies and laboratory practices
  • Passion for hands-on laboratory and pilot plant work, with willingness to work directly in industrial process environments
  • Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, and a continuous learning mindset
  • Excellent commitment to Environment, Health and Safety standards and practices
  • Strong communication and presentation skills in English
  • Proficiency with standard business and technical software tools such as Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and SAP
  • Ability to work effectively in diverse global teams and build strong collaborative relationships
  • Willingness to travel occasionally, primarily within Europe

How Would You Stand Out?

  • Hands-on experience in polymer chemistry, including synthesis, modification, and characterization of polymers and particle-based systems
  • Industrial experience with cellulose modification technologies, polysaccharides, hydrocolloids, polymerization processes, or related sustainable materials
  • Experience with data analysis, modelling, carbohydrate structural characterization, linkage analysis, derivatization techniques, external R&D collaborations, or custom manufacturing operations

Why Choose Us?

  • Work on innovative technologies that contribute to healthier and more sustainable products
  • Be part of a global R&D network with opportunities for international collaboration and exposure
  • Gain experience across the full development lifecycle from laboratory research to commercial manufacturing
  • Work in a highly skilled multidisciplinary team that values expertise, curiosity, and knowledge sharing
  • Develop professionally through challenging projects, mentoring, and continuous learning opportunities
  • Join a company committed to creating positive impact for people and the planet through science and innovation

🌍 Our Kantvik Research & Development Center is one of the key locations in IFF’s global network – a place where cutting‑edge research, industrial know‑how and innovation come together. Our team in Kantvik has developed numerous processes that have been implemented in global production facilities – including manufacturing technologies for various sweeteners and betaine. In Kantvik, you work with advanced technologies as part of an international scientific community, on projects with real impact. Join us in shaping the future of biotechnology!

The position is permanent, and the preferred start date is as soon as possible. Please submit your application through Workday by Oct 11, 2026. We review applications continuously and may begin interviews during the application period.

Please note that all applications must be submitted exclusively through our Workday recruitment system.

We are a global leader in taste, scent, and nutrition, offering our customers a broader range of natural solutions and accelerating our growth strategy. title: Rayonmanager
description:
Ben jij een inspirerende leider met ervaring in leidinggeven of coaching? Als Rayonmanager bij Basic-Fit speel jij een cruciale rol in het succes van onze clubs. Met jouw passie voor leiderschap zorg je ervoor dat jouw team excelleert op alle fronten, van Sales tot Service. Jij bent niet alleen een stuwende kracht achter je team, maar ook een voorbeeld van professionaliteit en betrokkenheid. Spreekt dit jou aan? Dan is de rol van Rayonmanager bij Basic-Fit in omgeving Oost-Nederland de perfecte uitdaging voor jou! Lees snel verder!

Dit bieden wij


Werken als Rayonmanager bij Basic-Fit betekent:

  • Bruto startsalaris van € 3.390,- per maand, op basis van een 40-urige werkweek;
  • Vakantietoeslag van 8%;
  • Deelname aan onze pensioenregeling (Basic-Fit betaalt 52% van de premie);
  • 25 vakantiedagen per jaar;
  • Feestdagentoeslag van 50%;
  • Een leaseauto;
  • Een laptop en mobiele telefoon.

De voordelen van werken bij Basic-Fit


● Bij Basic-Fit geloven we in jouw potentieel. Groei mee met ons mee als internationaal bedrijf en grijp de kans om door te groeien binnen onze organisatie. Je hebt onbeperkt toegang tot alle online trainingen van GoodHabitz.

● Je wordt onderdeel van de Orange Community waar diversiteit gevierd wordt en waar je jezelf mag zijn. Met de Orange Connect App ben je altijd verbonden en up-to-date.

● Wat is er beter dan werken in een omgeving waar gezondheid en fitness voorop staan? Maak gebruik van de mogelijkheid om zelf te sporten en ervaar de energieke en positieve werksfeer.

Zo ziet jouw functie eruit


Als Rayonmanager ben jij verantwoordelijk voor het realiseren van een maximaal resultaat van jouw cluster. Dit doe je door je te focussen op het behalen van de gestelde doelen op het gebied van Sales, Kwaliteit, Service, Hygiëne en Personeel. Daarnaast ben je verantwoordelijk voor het aansturen van de Teamleider(s) en Gastheren / Gastvrouwen. Je zorgt ervoor dat er goed functionerende teams op de clubs staan waarbij je de werkprocessen uitlegt en borgt op basis van de gestelde doelen. Je werkt diensten mee op diverse clubs om goed op de hoogte te blijven van de operationele werkzaamheden binnen jouw rayon.

Als Rayonmanager van Basic-Fit


  • Leid je de kwaliteit en ontwikkeling van je team, waarbij je coacht, motiveert en begeleidt, en indien nodig bijstuurt;
  • Zorg je voor een soepel verloop van werkprocessen bij de opening van nieuwe clubs;
  • Ben je verantwoordelijk voor de verkoop van producten en lidmaatschappen binnen jouw cluster, waarbij je jouw team motiveert;
  • Handel je adequaat bij calamiteiten, waarbij je de nodige acties afstemt met de Regio Manager en HR-adviseur;
  • Optimaliseer je de klanttevredenheid;
  • Communiceer je effectief en leg je organisatieprocessen duidelijk uit aan medewerkers om draagvlak te verkrijgen;
  • Werk je twee diensten per week op een van jouw clubs binnen jouw cluster;
  • Creëer je een positieve werksfeer en bevorder je de medewerkerstevredenheid in jouw cluster;
  • Ben je een voorbeeld voor anderen op het gebied van professionaliteit, houding en gedrag.

Wie zoeken wij?


Een proactieve en gedreven manager, met een scherp oog voor resultaat en de mens. Daarbij heb jij ervaring met leidinggeven of coaching en weet jij als geen ander hoe je een team kan motiveren.

Verder heb je:

  • Minimaal MBO+ werk- en denkniveau, opgedaan door werkervaring of opleiding;
  • Leidinggevende / coachende ervaring, bijvoorbeeld vanuit de retail of de sportclub;
  • Bij voorkeur een beschikbaarheid om 40 uur te werken, 32 uur is bespreekbaar;
  • Communicatief sterk, dit betekent dat je je goed kan uitdrukken en je goed kan schrijven;
  • Je schakelt snel tussen beleid en operationele zaken;
  • Rijbewijs B.

Over Basic-Fit


Basic-Fit is een dynamisch en sterk groeiende organisatie met een duidelijke missie. Inmiddels zijn wij de grootste fitness keten van Europa. Buiten Nederland hebben we clubs in België, Duitsland, Luxemburg, Frankrijk en Spanje. Ons doel is om de komende jaren verder te professionaliseren en door te groeien. Mede dankzij jouw inzet kunnen we onze groei realiseren en dat geeft weer nieuwe mogelijkheden voor jouw carrière om hierin mee te groeien!

Basic-Fit zet zich daarnaast in om een inclusieve werkgever te zijn die gelijke kansen biedt voor iedereen. Of je nu één van onze leden of medewerkers bent, wij hebben aandacht voor jouw welzijn en focussen ons op diversiteit! Waar je ook voor gaat, wij zijn er om je te ondersteunen en je te helpen met #becomfortable te voelen. Zo kun jij de wereld aan!

Klaar voor de uitdaging? Solliciteer direct!


Ben je geïnteresseerd in de functie van Rayonmanager? Solliciteer dan via de sollicitatiebutton rechtsboven.

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

Okta's Customer Identity Cloud (CIC), powered by Auth0 technology, is an easy to implement authentication and authorization platform designed by developers for developers. We make access to applications safe, secure, and seamless for more than 100 million daily logins around the world. Our modern approach to identity enables this Tier-0 global service to deliver convenience, privacy, and security so customers can focus on innovation.

The Services Architect - CIAM is a technical authority on both cloud and on-premises based IT systems and is responsible for ensuring the successful design and implementation of Okta’s industry leading cloud identity platform at our customers. You will focus on Okta’s CIAM offering targeted at customer identity use cases. You will develop relationships with customers to help them achieve their business goals while promoting creative solutions. You will establish yourself as a trusted partner with your customers with a focus on their success. You will translate business needs and insights into an actionable strategy and assist customers in driving their initiatives to results and high business value. This role is for the Customer Identity Cloud product unit and you’ll be supporting CIC customers.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Review and lead the gathering of business, functional and technical requirements for establishing an Identity platform powered by Okta for our customers.

title: Quality Assurer
description:
Job Description

To promote and uphold operational excellence by conducting structured quality assessments, identifying gaps, and ensuring adherence to defined standards, policies and procedures. The role supports continuous improvement by analysing quality outcomes, facilitating corrective actions, and strengthening process integrity. Enable a positive customer experience by ensuring consistent, accurate and well‑controlled operational execution.
  • Conduct routine, systematic quality reviews across operational processes to ensure compliance with approved standards, internal policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Identify non‑conformances, defects, and process deviations, documenting findings with clarity, accuracy and actionable detail.
  • Maintain up‑to‑date quality records, assessment outcomes and audit trails to support governance and reporting requirements.
  • Analyse recurring quality issues, emerging trends and root causes, and escalate insights to management for decision‑making and process optimisation.
  • Prepare clear, concise quality reports, dashboards and summaries for operational teams and leadership.
  • Support the implementation of continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing defects, enhancing process efficiency and improving customer outcomes.
  • Participate in testing and validation of new processes, systems or changes to ensure quality implications are identified before rollout.
  • Provide direct feedback, coaching and guidance to frontline staff to help correct errors, reinforce best practices and strengthen process adherence.
  • Ensure operational teams understand quality standards and consistently apply them in day‑to‑day activities.
  • Serve as a liaison between operational teams, quality governance bodies and leadership by communicating insights, risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Maintain and update quality documentation (e.g., checklists, scoring guides, assessment templates) to ensure alignment with changing processes.
  • Support calibration activities to ensure consistent scoring and interpretation of quality outcomes across assessors and business units.
  • Apply recognised quality methodologies including root‑cause analysis and continuous improvement frameworks to strengthen the integrity of quality findings.
  • Gather and analyse customer feedback, survey results and related data to identify service gaps, trends and improvement opportunities.
  • Support market and competitor analysis where customer experience or quality implications exist.
  • Contribute to aligning operational processes with customer expectations and internal service standards.
  • Identify potential risks, control weaknesses or process inefficiencies and recommend corrective actions.
  • Support monitoring activities that ensure compliance with internal governance, risk management policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Promote a culture of proactive risk awareness and quality consciousness within operational teams.
  • Monitoring Interactions:Regularly reviewing interactions, to assess agent performance against established criteria. This helps identify adherence to scripts, proper handling of issues, and overall client service effectiveness.
  • Performance Analysis: Analysing data from monitored interactions, alongside key performance indicators (KPIs), to spot trends, recurring issues, and areas needing attention

title: Senior Director, HR-Front Line Care
description:
This is where your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Your role at Baxter:


Develop and implement the human resources strategy for Front Line Care in support of the business unit’s growth, innovation, quality and margin objectives and the desired Baxter culture. Serve as the principal HR advisor and coach to the President of Front Line Care and the FLC leadership team on organizational design, workforce planning, talent management and development, leadership effectiveness, total rewards, employee relations and change management.


As a member of the Baxter HR Leadership Team, contribute to the shaping of enterprise people strategy, standards and HR operating model — not only its adoption within FLC. Success in this role requires strategic oversight and design capability coupled with the credibility and appetite to drive tactical execution personally and through a team, in a matrixed, highly regulated, multi-site environment.


Organizational Relationships

  • Reports to: Chief Human Resources Officer, Baxter International.
  • Business Partner for President, Front Line Care.
  • Supports Front Line Care LT/direct reports to President
  • Leads: a team of HR Business Partners and HR professionals supporting FLC commercial, R&D, operations, quality/regulatory and enabling functions.
  • Peers: HR leaders for Care & Connectivity Solutions, Medical Products & Therapies, Global Operations, and the enterprise functions; leaders of the Talent, Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, HR Operations/People Services, HR Strategy, HRIS, and People Relations Centers of Excellence.
  • Key business interfaces: FLC Finance, Legal and Compliance, Communications, Quality & Regulatory, Global Operations and Supply Chain, and regional/country HR leadership.

Essential Responsibilities


Business Partnership & People Strategy

  • Translate business strategy into a people strategy. Develop, gain alignment on and execute a multi-year HR plan for FLC that is explicitly tied to revenue growth, innovation pipeline, quality, service and margin commitments; monitor its effectiveness continuously and pivot as conditions change.
  • Act as a full member of the business leadership team. Contribute to commercial, operational and investment decisions with an independent point of view, not only on the people implications of decisions already made.
  • Develop organization strategy. Identify and research human resources issues affecting the business; contribute information, analysis and recommendations to strategic direction; establish HR objectives in line with organizational objectives.
  • Represent FLC into enterprise HR. Bring business-unit requirements into the design of enterprise HR programs, and act as an owner of enterprise HR outcomes as a member of the HR Leadership Team.
  • Establish effective operating processes with the leadership team — including prioritization, resource allocation, decision rights, operating rhythm and governance — and drive the organizational alignment that enables strong partnership with functions inside and outside the business unit.

Organization Design, Effectiveness & Workforce Planning

  • Continually assess the effectiveness of the business model and organizational dynamics and lead efforts to realign or refocus structure, roles, spans and layers, and accountabilities as needed.
  • Lead organization design work across a complex, multi-site, matrixed footprint spanning R&D, regulated manufacturing, quality, commercial and service, balancing global consistency against local and regulatory requirements.
  • Own strategic workforce planning for FLC: capability gap analysis, build/buy/borrow decisions, critical role identification, location and footprint strategy, and cost-to-serve; partner with Finance on headcount planning, productivity targets and the annual operating plan.
  • Design and lead restructuring and cost actions where required — including consultation processes, selection criteria, risk mitigation, and the leadership and communication plans that protect delivery and morale through change.
  • Partner with the leadership team on team effectiveness — diagnosing leadership team dynamics, clarifying accountability, and facilitating interventions that improve how the top team operates.

Talent Management, Development & Succession

  • Own the talent agenda for the business unit: talent reviews, calibration, succession planning for critical and executive roles, and accelerated development plans for high-potential talent.
  • Build technical and leadership capability in scarce, competitive skill areas relevant to FLC — including software and connected-device engineering, data and AI, systems and hardware engineering, regulatory and quality, and clinical and commercial excellence.
  • Partner with Talent Acquisition and Executive Search on executive staffing, pipeline strategy, employer brand in key geographies, and the quality and speed of senior hiring decisions.
  • Drive performance management across the business unit: goal setting, ongoing feedback, year-end review, differentiation of performance, and management of underperformance.
  • Champion career pathing, internal mobility and retention for critical talent, using data to anticipate flight risk rather than react to it.


Executive Coaching & Leadership Development

  • Proactively coach senior leaders — including the FLC President and their direct reports — on leadership effectiveness, executive presence, decision making, team building and personal development, offering candid counsel and constructive challenge.
  • Assess leadership capability against current and future business requirements and act decisively where capability, capacity or behavior does not meet the standard.
  • Onboard and integrate senior hires and newly promoted leaders to accelerate their time to contribution.


Culture, Engagement & Change

  • Shape and reinforce the desired culture across the business unit, translating Baxter’s mission and values — courage, trust, collaboration, ownership and accountability for results — into observable leadership behaviors and management practice.
  • Lead the engagement agenda: survey design input, interpretation of results, action planning with leaders, and follow-through that is measured rather than assumed.
  • Serve as change leader for major business transitions — operating model shifts, systems implementations, site changes, portfolio moves and integration activity — including stakeholder analysis, communication planning and leader enablement, in partnership with Communications.
  • Advance diversity, equity and inclusion within the business unit through representation goals, inclusive hiring and development practice, and accountability in talent processes.


Total Rewards, Recognition & Performance

  • Drive an effective reward and recognition strategy that reinforces the culture and behaviors the business needs, in partnership with the Total Rewards COE.
  • Partner on compensation planning and governance: annual merit and bonus cycles, long-term incentive allocation, executive compensation recommendations, sales incentive plan design input, job architecture and leveling, and market competitiveness in key talent markets.
  • Ensure pay decisions are defensible — internally equitable, externally competitive, and consistent with Baxter policy and applicable pay transparency and pay equity regulation.


Employee Relations, Labor & Compliance

  • Provide coaching and consultation on employee relations matters, including complex and escalated cases, investigations, performance and conduct issues, and separations; partner with Legal, Compliance and the ER COE on risk assessment and resolution.
  • Oversee labor and works council relationships relevant to the business unit’s footprint, including consultation and information obligations in applicable international jurisdictions.
  • Ensure HR practices meet the requirements of a regulated medical device environment, including training, qualification and documentation expectations under the quality management system, and cooperation with internal and external audits.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable employment law and Baxter policy across all countries in scope, and escalate systemic risk appropriately.


Portfolio Actions and Integration

  • Act as HR lead for inorganic activity affecting the business unit — acquisitions, divestitures, partnerships and integrations — covering due diligence, organization and leadership design, retention strategy, harmonization of rewards and policy, culture integration and Day 1 readiness.
  • Own the people workstream of post-close integration plans, including synergy commitments, and track realization against them.


HR Team Leadership & Functional Excellence

  • Lead, develop and inspire the FLC HR team, setting direction and standards, building business acumen and consulting capability, managing performance and building bench strength within the HR function.
  • Ensure effective delivery through the HR operating model, holding a clear interface with COEs, HR Operations and regional HR so the business receives coordinated rather than fragmented support.
  • Model hands-on execution. Operate fluidly between strategic design and personal delivery of the work, particularly where the organization is lean or the issue is high-stakes.


Data, Analytics & Measurement

  • Develop and implement measurement systems to determine the impact of HR programs, and report on them to business and HR leadership.
  • Use workforce data and analytics — turnover and regretted attrition, internal fill rate, time to fill, span and layer, engagement, diversity representation, cost per head and productivity — to diagnose issues and make evidence-based recommendations.
  • Set and track people KPIs as part of the business unit’s operating review, holding the same rigor as commercial and financial metrics.

The Consultant Government Grants (“Consultant”) will be responsible for researching and preparing all hiring and training grants for all clients, and assist with the compliance reporting post grant approvals. In addition, the Consultant will assist Managers and Senior Consultants with researching appropriate grants for client initiatives, developing funding analysis reports and monitoring deliverables. The Consultant will also be responsible for researching, updating and maintaining the Firm’s Grant Program Database. This will include continually researching new and existing programs, entering updates and reporting status changes to the team. The position will demand an attention to detail and the ability to multi-task in a constantly changing environment.

Job Profile Summary


The Consultant Government Grants (“Consultant”) will be responsible for writing and preparing business proposals and funding applications that range from $5,000 to $20,000,000 in size and complete compliance reporting as required. These funding applications are positioned to assist our clients’ businesses with projects including business expansion, research & development, capital investment, and HR initiatives.

The Consultant will also support Managers and Senior Consultants with developing supplemental documentation, including business plans, budgets, and financial information for client initiatives, and monitoring deliverables, updating, and maintaining the Firm’s Program knowledge and systems. The position will demand attention to detail and the ability to multi-task in a constantly changing environment.


Duties and Responsibilities:

Preparation and Submission of Business Cases and Funding Proposals (90%): Work directly with Managers and clients on the preparation and submission of funding proposals. This includes synthesizing project information gathered from research, client meetings, notes from the sales team or manager, and previous funding proposals. We typically write 90%+ of content in a written submission up to 100 pages.

Tasks include:

  • Application Preparation/Writing: Applications include varying combinations of a project and/or business focus depending on the nature of the request for funding. You will work with your team to write drafts and/or review business plans and/or formal application files, including reviewing financial statements and forecasts.
  • Research and Analysis: Research through a variety of online sources, market reports, client data, and interview notes to develop a coherent narrative for a funding proposal.
  • Compliance: Assist with the compliance and reporting requirements post grant approval.
  • Systemization/Document Management: As documentation (e.g. financial statements, quotes, etc.) for a project comes in, you are responsible for filing and storing the documents appropriately on our system. Additionally, the Consultant is responsible for maintaining the integrity and consistency of our file management system.

Other (10%): Support administrative and other duties as required by the Firm. This can include:

  • Administrative Support: CRM and other systems recordkeeping, emails, and reporting to Managers.
  • Internal & External Meetings: Meeting prep and facilitation for client meetings and weekly team meetings.
  • New Program Research: Support Managers and other team members to complete new program research, and changes to existing programs. Reaching out to programs to obtain program information may be required.
  • Other: Special projects may be assigned on an on-going basis, these can include blog writing, marketing support, systems development, etc.

Education:


A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Humanities, Social Sciences, Business/Administration, Journalism, Accounting, or Science is required.

Qualifications - Required:


  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
  • 1+ years of experience in industry; various experience acceptable
  • Strong decision-making skills: ability to work with limited information
  • Experience in business case writing
  • Ability to work under pressure and tight timelines
  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills
  • Ability to think outside the box

Qualifications - Preferred:


  • Experience in proposal writing
  • Experience preparing business and marketing plans
  • Industry experience in roles that include strategic planning, project management, or similar. Ideally experience in a manufacturing or advanced technology sector
  • Understanding of accounting and finance practices; ability to interpret an income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement.

Computer Skills:



To perform this job successfully, an individual must have intermediate knowledge of Microsoft® Word, Excel, Power Point, Outlook, and Internet navigation and research.

Certificates and Licenses:

Valid driver’s license required.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

title: Field Credit Officer (Anambra)
description:
About Us:

Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere.

Job Title: Field Credit Officer

Reports to: Regional Credit Manager

Employment Type: Outsourced

Work Mode: Onsite

About this role:

As a Field Credit Officer, you would be saddled with the duty of onboarding and managing businesses that would access our credit products. You would be tasked with growing your loan portfolio while maintaining profitability by ensuring that all loans are repaid as and when due. As a result, you would play a vital role in the assessment of these businesses during their credit application and leverage innovative tools we have developed to help you monitor their performance during the course of the loan.

You would also be responsible for making deductions from several information sources about the 5Cs of credit, with capacity, character, and capital as major priorities. Make recommendations to management before, during, and after the disbursement of a loan facility as to the best actions to be taken, considering several economic factors.

Responsibilities:

  • Identify and onboard viable businesses within your assigned geographical area to open business accounts with Moniepoint
  • Engage customers to ensure optimal usage of accounts to allow them to qualify for access to credit
  • Review and approve (or decline) loan requests by thoroughly analyzing all the data available
  • Embark on physical visitation to potential borrowers’ business places for evaluation of business books, taking inventory and turnover into consideration
  • Meet gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets by maintaining a healthy number of loan customers while ensuring that all loans in portfolio are performing
  • Monitor active loan portfolio to ensure continued use of business account and loan repayment performance
  • Perform all other credit-related functions as may be assigned by a supervisor

Experience & Background:

  • Minimum of an OND in any business-related discipline
  • Minimum of 2 years’ experience in a sales role for credit products in a financial institution
  • Demonstrable knowledge of credit risk analysis
  • Good knowledge of financial analysis is an added advantage
  • Must be resident in Anambra

Skills & Competencies:

  • Apt attention to details
  • Proven simple/complex analytical skills
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Agility and perseverance

What success looks like in this role:

  • Consistent achievement of gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets.
  • Maintaining a healthy, performing loan portfolio with minimized default rates through rigorous physical visitations and monitoring.
  • Successful onboarding and engagement of viable businesses that actively utilize Moniepoint business accounts.
  • Accurate credit risk assessments based on key factors like capacity, character, and capital.

Why join us:

  • Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.
  • Opportunity to work with Africa’s fastest-growing fintech and make a direct impact on business growth across the region.

This employee will be a member of the HPC team and will support SpaceX personnel and proprietary systems. The ideal candidate will be flexible and flourish in a fast paced and challenging environment. They should be a self-starter, self-motivator and possess ingenuity to excel at this position.

  • Install and integrate Linux-based compute clusters
  • Write instructional documentation and convey highly technical ideas in non-technical terms

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience with client and server hardware/software, management tools, enterprise networking, virtualization, and security technologies

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 5+ years of professional experience building, deploying and troubleshooting Linux systems
  • Experience with a scripting language (Bash, Python) to automate and solve reoccurring tasks
  • Experience building, deploying and troubleshooting HPC clusters
  • Familiarity with cluster resource managers (Slurm, PBS, LSF)
  • Experience with monitoring and alerting technologies (Prometheus, Grafana, Nagios)
  • Familiarity with scientific and engineering computing (CFD, FEA)
  • Familiarity with large scale AI training
  • Familiarity with GPU usage in a compute cluster and Cuda
  • Experience with containers (Docker, Podman, Singularity)
  • Experience deploying and maintaining automated configuration management software (Puppet, Ansible)
  • Comfortable working with mission critical and sensitive systems, with a sense of urgency appropriate to the responsibilities
  • Eligibility for access to classified material up to TS/SCI with Polygraph
  • Experience with Kubernetes

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed

title: Field Credit Officer (Abia)
description:

Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere.

Employment Type: Outsourced

Work Mode: Onsite

About this role:

As a Field Credit Officer, you would be saddled with the duty of onboarding and managing businesses that would access our credit products. You would be tasked with growing your loan portfolio while maintaining profitability by ensuring that all loans are repaid as and when due. As a result, you would play a vital role in the assessment of these businesses during their credit application and leverage innovative tools we have developed to help you monitor their performance during the course of the loan.

You would also be responsible for making deductions from several information sources about the 5Cs of credit, with capacity, character, and capital as major priorities.   • Identify and onboard viable businesses within your assigned geographical area to open business accounts with Moniepoint
  • Engage customers to ensure optimal usage of accounts to allow them to qualify for access to credit
  • Review and approve (or decline) loan requests by thoroughly analyzing all the data available
  • Embark on physical visitation to potential borrowers’ business places for evaluation of business books, taking inventory and turnover into consideration
  • Meet gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets by maintaining a healthy number of loan customers while ensuring that all loans in portfolio are performing
  • Monitor active loan portfolio to ensure continued use of business account and loan repayment performance
  • Perform all other credit-related functions as may be assigned by a supervisor

Experience & Background:

  • Minimum of an OND in any business-related discipline
  • Minimum of 2 years’ experience in a sales role for credit products in a financial institution
  • Demonstrable knowledge of credit risk analysis
  • Good knowledge of financial analysis is an added advantage
  • Must be resident in Abia - Ohafia, Osisioma, Abia North, and Abia Central

Skills & Competencies:

  • Apt attention to details
  • Proven simple/complex analytical skills
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Agility and perseverance

What success looks like in this role:

  • Consistent achievement of gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets.
  • Maintaining a healthy, performing loan portfolio with minimized default rates through rigorous physical visitations and monitoring.
  • Successful onboarding and engagement of viable businesses that actively utilize Moniepoint business accounts.
  • Accurate credit risk assessments based on key factors like capacity, character, and capital.

Why join us:

  • Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.
  • Opportunity to work with Africa’s fastest-growing fintech and make a direct impact on business growth across the region.

title: GNOC Tier II Incident Management Technician
description:
The Digital Modernization Sector at Leidos is seeking a Tier II Incident Management Technician to support computer data communications systems, providing network event management and incident troubleshooting. Technicians provide additional support by ensuring network devices meet baseline configurations, software, and network performance standards. Technicians will make extensive use of Microfocus tools, ServiceNow, and knowledge of the various levels of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model to complete daily network Operations and Maintenance (O&M) tasks. This is a day time Panama Shift with a 6am-6pm schedule.


The job duties of the GNOC Tier II Incident Management Technician are as follows:

  • Support the installation and maintenance of the client Local Area Network (LAN)/Wide Area Network (WAN) devices.

  • Administer networks including hardware, systems software, applications software, and all hardware configurations.
  • Coordinate network operations, maintenance, repairs, or upgrades.
  • Perform configuration management functions such as validating topology drawings and ensure that asset management records are accurate.
  • Leverage knowledge of OSI layers 1, 2, and 3 to troubleshoot various network faults and performance issues
  • Configure and troubleshoot layer two switching (Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs))
  • Modify and troubleshoot layer three routing across the enterprise network.
  • Conduct extensive troubleshooting of Multiprotocol Label Switch (MPLS) across the WAN.
  • Participate in evaluation of new network technologies and provide recommendations to the network architecture team regarding the integration of these technologies into the existing network.
  • Ensure adequacy of plans for hardware and communications. Develop and implement methodologies for analysis, testing, and support of LAN and WAN networks.
  • Leverage various network tools such as Microfocus and Riverbed to quickly identify and isolate customer impacting events on the network.
  • Communicate and troubleshoot with vendors and other service providers to efficiently resolve incidents.
  • Diagnose hardware and software problems and coordinate the replacement of defective components.

  • Candidate must have 10 years of experience that can be a combination of work history and education. This equates to a doctorate and 3 years, a master’s and 4 years, a bachelor’s and 6 years, an associates and 8 years or HS diploma and 10 years.

Leads enterprise data governance support.

  • Leads the development and maintenance of metadata repositories and management systems (data catalog).
  • Performs advanced non-technical tool configuration within the Data Catalog, including complex Catalog UI, Templates, Terms/Glossaries, and Data Asset Curation.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

CDMP (Certified Data Management Professional-Practitioner or Master), Certified Data Governance & Stewardship Professional (DGSP) from ICCP (Institute for Certification of Computing Professionals), or other Data Governance Certification (DGQP) preferred.

title: Offensive Cyberspace Operational Planner, Journeyman
description:
Job Description

Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?


At Leidos, we deliver innovative solutions through the efforts of our diverse and talented people who are dedicated to our customers’ success. We empower our teams, contribute to our communities, and operate sustainably. Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people, and our community. The Leidos National Security Sector (NSS) combines technology-enabled services and mission software capabilities in the areas of cyber, logistics, security operations, and decision analytics to support our defense and intel customers’ mission to defend against evolving threats around the world.


Your greatest work is ahead!


The Intelligence Sector seeks highly qualified and trained Journeyman-level Offensive Cyberspace Operational Planners to support Department of Defense Joint Planning processes that underpin United States Cyber Command (USCYBERCOM) operations, with focus on supporting power projection in and through cyberspace in support of Combatant Commander and National objectives. Individuals will engage in Cyberspace Operational Planning activities supporting Leidos on-site contract support to USCYBERCOM J3 (Operations), Cyber National Mission Force (CNMF), and Joint Task Force-Ares (JTF-ARES).


This opportunity is in anticipation of a potential future contract award.


What you’ll be doing:

  • Engage in approved plans development and staffing processes within collaborative environment to enable range of Cyberspace Operations (CO) according to USCYBERCOM planning guidance and applicable Joint publications.
  • Develop and synchronize Offensive Cyberspace Operational (OCO) plans to deliver integrated cyber effects against adversary systems in support of Joint and National strategic objectives.
  • Support targeting selection, validation, synchronization, and enable integration during the execution of activities within Cyber Warfare domain
  • Draft and staff foundational planning documents such as Operational Plans (OPLANS), Operational Orders (OPORDs), and Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs).
  • Support Joint Operational Planning Groups and Teams (OPG/OPT), and develop and integrate Cyberspace capabilities into plans.
  • Develop concepts of support, courses of action, integrate command and external capabilities, coordinate and document comprehensive plans.
  • Engage in, and provide situational awareness to, range of projects, Crisis Action Teams, and current operations activities supporting OPTs.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of cyber threats and attack methods and techniques emanating from state and non-state adversaries and tiered vulnerabilities within Blue Space as focus of threats.
  • Review, approve, prioritize, and submit operational requirements for research, development, and/or acquisition of cyber capabilities.
  • Analyze and assess internal and external partner CO capabilities and tools.
  • Transition operational planning efforts to current operations.
  • Navigate organizational structure as it pertains to full spectrum CO, including the functions, responsibilities, and interrelationships among distinct internal elements.
  • Integrate and synchronize intelligence planning activities with operational planning timelines.
  • Conduct long-range, strategic planning efforts with internal and external partners in cyber activities.
  • Communicate complex information, concepts, or ideas in a confident and well-organized manner through verbal, written, and/or visual means.

What does Leidos need from me?

  • Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility and Polygraph required.
  • BA/BS degree within Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or relevant field of study.
  • 8 plus years recent (since 2018) work experience as CO Planner; can waive two years of experience requirement for every year spent on a Combat Mission Team (CMT) in any work role.
  • Demonstrated familiarity with OCO concepts, capabilities, and authorities (Title 10 vs. Title 50, and familiarity with military operations including phases of planning, approval, and execution.
  • Intimate familiarity with applicable Joint Publications.
  • Formal training as Cyber Operational Planner within Department of Defense or Intelligence Community.
  • Broad knowledge of Blue-space Cyber capabilities and demonstrate understanding of available Cyber infrastructure or platforms to conduct OCO.
  • Knowledge of the range of CO and their underlying intelligence support needs, topics, and focus areas.
  • Knowledge of computer networking fundamentals as well as concepts, terminology, and operations of a wide range of communications media (computer and telephone networks, satellite, fiber, wireless).
  • Ability to support timely, accurate, relevant analytical production, to include documents, summaries, issue papers, talking points, and briefings.
  • Demonstrated proficiency working in a fast-paced collaborative environment, ability to proactively multi-task and meet short deadlines.
  • Able to work across Department of Defense and Intelligence Community agencies to support organizational goals.

Favorable if you have:

  • Masters’ Degree within Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or relevant field of study.
  • Familiarity with USCYBERCOM organizational structure and mission.
  • Prior experience supporting Joint operations across multiple warfighting domains.
  • Demonstrated experience incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into operations at any level to increase efficiency and effectiveness of operational outcomes.
  • Experience with Space-enabled CO.
  • Joint Professional Military Education, Phase II (JPME II) graduate, or civilian equivalency.
  • Formal training within field of Cyber Warfare and Joint Operations.
  • Completion of Service-specific or Joint Cyberspace Operational Planning courses, such as Army Cyberspace Operations Planners Course or Joint Cyberspace Operations Planners Course.
  • Familiar with art of Data Science and applicability to CO.
  • Familiar with Microsoft Power BI data visualization software.
  • Desired Certifications: DoD 8570 IAT Level II (CCNA Security, COMPTIA CySA+, COMPTIA Security + CE, GICSP, GSEC, SSCP).


If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

title: Specialist, Shelter Engagement  - Central Arkansas
description:
Location: Remote in Central Arkansas - candidate will need to be located in Little Rock and surrounding areas (travel is expected to be up to 75% within the region)

Hiring Range: This position’s hiring range is anticipated to start at $58,656 annually, plus great benefits!



Prison Break. Breakout. Fixer Upper. This Old House.

Imagine if there was a job where day-to-day was a combination of these types of shows, but you were assisting dogs and cats to bust out of traditional shelters, where staff love them but often don’t have enough resources to save them. Then you get to share the resources we have to help the shelters enhance their facilities and programs.


So, not only do you get to help dogs and cats, but you also get to help the staff who try so hard and care so much by giving them support to improve their shelter, make their jobs more rewarding, and to save more animals.


Shelter Engagement Specialists are on the front line of lifesaving. They play a direct role in achieving Best Friends Animal Society’s no-kill mission by selecting and pulling animals from priority shelters, and then helping priority shelter partners make enhancements to their shelter as well as develop or enhance lifesaving programming.


We’re seeking someone who has experience working in animal shelters, is savvy with dogs, cats, and PEOPLE, loves problem solving, and is not afraid to get covered in fur to bring about the future of animal sheltering. Does this sound like a dream job to you? If so, apply today for the Shelter Engagement Specialist role and make that dream a reality!

Culture Statement and Responsibility: We believe in treating everyone with kindness and compassion, building trust through authenticity and following through on commitments. We prioritize well-being alongside our mission, fostering strong relationships through open communication and transparent feedback. Diversity and inclusion are integral to our culture, enriching team dynamics by valuing diverse perspectives. Each team member is responsible for creating an inclusive environment where all voices are respected and contributing to a workplace that embodies our shared values and commitment to progress. By consistently aligning our actions with our Guiding Principles, we strengthen our culture and ensure that our values are lived every day.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Demonstrate kindness and the Golden Rule in our everyday actions by practicing inclusion and respect for every person for the value they bring to the table. Be a role model for the spirit of authenticity, kindness, and positive influence with each other, our visitors, volunteers, and the animals every day. This includes listening, being present, being supportive of others, and demonstrating compassion and curiosity in conflict.
  • Build relationships with assigned shelters and provide consultative guidance, coaching and strategic mentorship on an ongoing basis to help shelters implement programming to achieve and sustain a 90% save rate. These areas include; shelter operations, lifesaving programs and proven strategies, community engagement, and more; including participating in direct, hands-on lifesaving work at partner shelter locations, as well as virtually
  • Travel to shelters to evaluate population needs and placement opportunities for dogs and cats for our Northwest Arkansas program and safely transport them to the center.
  • Support partner shelters by partnering with shelter leaders and staff to assess day-to-day operational challenges, reinforce accountability, and guide adoption of effective lifesaving practices as needed to provide needed lifesaving training to help them achieve and sustain no-kill; participate in team-building activities with shelter staff as needed to enhance buy-in.
  • Deliver superior customer service to partner shelters, community stakeholders and others. Develop and maintain a robust knowledge of Best Friends’ and animal welfare standard best practices to support lifesaving and care.
  • Serve as a mission ambassador, representing Best Friends’ mission and vision within partner shelters; leading training, consultation, and mentoring efforts; developing and refining resources for partner shelters on proven programs support their success in achieving no-kill; support the maintenance of statistics within priority partners shelters.
  • Lead and empower volunteers and volunteer teams in support of programs with the goal of utilizing volunteers to the greatest extent possible to expand Best Friends lifesaving capacity; deliver and lead superior customer service.
  • Work collaboratively with and assist Best Friends’ team members in all areas of operations to develop, refine, and implement efficient processes to achieve lifesaving goals exercise judgment in prioritizing work, follow policies, procedures, and task lists, including accurate and timely communications, work completion, data entry, and recordkeeping; respect partner policies when working in partner facilities.
  • Travel up to 75% within the state of Arkansas and surrounding states.

Skills and Experience:

  • Background in animal sheltering working in an animal shelter is required, preferably in a municipal, government or private shelter with contractual animal control responsibilities.
  • Basic ability to identify and speak to medical and behavioral characteristics, as well as body language of dogs and cats.
  • Ability to work in an environment that is not no-kill, remaining professional, nonjudgmental, and supportive of that shelter’s staff.
  • Experience with and comfortability driving large multi-passenger vehicles or willingness to learn.
  • Experience leading teams and implementing programs is preferred but not required.
  • Bilingual or multilingual skills are preferred but not required.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, a team player, personable, professional, and able to get along with people from different backgrounds, as well as the ability to handle sensitive and confidential situations.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with well-developed organization skills to juggle multiple competing tasks and demands.
  • Resourceful, get-it-done attitude; initiative to assist in any area or process; problem solving, seeking answers independently and enthusiastically; flexibility to persist until goals are achieved.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office products; familiarity with shelter software/animal management software, or desire to learn.
  • Ability to professionally advocate Best Friends’ positions on issues; experience in supporting, engaging with, and developing relationships with volunteers and donors.

Physical Requirements:


  • Must have a valid driver's license for at least 3 years, ability to qualify to be added to Best Friends insurance.
  • Must be able to travel regularly up to 75% for evaluating and transporting pets, in shelter presentations, and training. Overnight stays when needed.
  • Exposure to dogs and cats of all sizes, temperaments, and medical status. Ability to work with, leash, kennel, walk, and handle cats and dogs, including those with health and/or behavior conditions/concerns.
  • Ability to be in a shelter environment and work in the presence of both cats and dogs, including large numbers of cats and dogs as in a shelter setting, and in shelters that are not yet no-kill.
  • Work indoors and outdoors in a variety of weather conditions including extreme heat and cold.
  • Must be able to routinely lift 40 pounds and perform daily strenuous activity including, but not limited to lifting, carrying, reaching, stooping, squatting, cleaning, and bending. Perform repetitive tasks for extended periods of time including typing, arm, and hand motion. Standing, sitting, or walking for prolonged periods of time.
  • Daily hours and days of the week may vary according to the needs of the department schedule; position includes weekends, nights, and holiday work.

description:

Leidos is seeking Distribution Engineers & Designers in Chicago, IL who are passionate about electric utility design engineering. We’re looking for someone who is dedicated to ensuring that every project, no matter how simple or complex, is of exceptional quality. You'll be working directly with clients to make sure that Leidos' reputation for high-quality work is always maintained. If you join us in this role, you'll gain expertise in a variety of areas, including NESC, Structural Pole Modeling, Electrical Power Calculations, GIS design training, Field Data Collection, and Client Design Standards. Your greatest work is ahead!


This position is hybrid in nature, where 3 days/week are spent working in our office, collaborating with internal teams, and 2 days/week can be spent working remotely.


As a Distribution Engineer / Designer, you can expect to:

  • Perform design engineering for Leidos electric utility customers
  • Develop work packages for OH, UG, URD, and Make Ready, using customer GIS and WMS systems such as EFD, AUD, Smallworld, ArcGIS, Infor, EAM, STORMS, and Maximo
